jushichijo_kenpo.title: Seventeen-Article Constitution
jushichijo_kenpo.caption: Rules for officials said to be set by Prince Shotoku. It opens with "Harmony is to be valued" and urges respect for Buddhism.

kenzuishi.title: Envoys Sent to Sui China
kenzuishi.caption: Ono no Imoko and others went to Sui to learn its advanced systems and culture. A letter from "the Son of Heaven where the sun rises" angered the emperor.

taika_no_kaishin.title: Taika Reform
taika_no_kaishin.caption: Reforms begun after Prince Naka no Oe and Nakatomi no Kamatari overthrew the Soga. They aimed at a state where the emperor ruled all land and people.

hakusonko.title: Battle of Baekgang
hakusonko.caption: A Yamato fleet sent to help restore Baekje was crushed by Tang and Silla. Afterward Japan worked to strengthen its own defenses.

jinshin_no_ran.title: Jinshin War
jinshin_no_ran.caption: A succession war after Emperor Tenji died. His brother Prince Oama defeated Tenji's son Prince Otomo and took the throne as Emperor Tenmu.

taiho_ritsuryo.title: Taiho Code
taiho_ritsuryo.caption: Compiled by Prince Osakabe and Fujiwara no Fuhito, Japan's first full code of penal and civil law. It set up the ritsuryo state.

heijokyo_sento.title: Capital Moved to Heijo-kyo
heijokyo_sento.caption: Empress Genmei moved the capital from Fujiwara-kyo to Heijo-kyo in Nara. Laid out on a grid like Tang's Chang'an, it was the stage of the Nara period.

kojiki.title: Kojiki Completed
kojiki.caption: Japan's oldest surviving history, written by O no Yasumaro from tales memorized by Hieda no Are. It runs from the age of gods to Empress Suiko.

nihon_shoki.title: Nihon Shoki Completed
nihon_shoki.caption: The first official history, compiled by Prince Toneri and others. Written in Chinese, it records events year by year from the age of gods to Empress Jito.

konden_einen.title: Law on Permanent Ownership of New Fields
konden_einen.caption: Newly cleared land could be kept forever. Public ownership of land broke down, paving the way for the later private estates (shoen).

daibutsu_kaigen.title: Eye-Opening of the Great Buddha
daibutsu_kaigen.caption: A ceremony for the Nara Great Buddha built at Emperor Shomu's wish. A monk from India painted in its eyes before some 10,000 monks.

heiankyo_sento.title: Capital Moved to Heian-kyo
heiankyo_sento.caption: Emperor Kanmu moved the capital from Nagaoka-kyo to Kyoto, away from the power of the temples. It stayed the capital for a thousand years.

kentoshi_haishi.title: Envoys to Tang Ended
kentoshi_haishi.caption: Sugawara no Michizane advised stopping the missions, citing Tang's decline and the dangerous voyage. A distinctly Japanese culture then grew.

kokin_wakashu.title: Kokin Wakashu Compiled
kokin_wakashu.caption: The first imperial poetry anthology, compiled by Ki no Tsurayuki and others for Emperor Daigo. Its kana preface is a classic essay on poetry.

michinaga_sessho.title: Fujiwara no Michinaga Becomes Regent
michinaga_sessho.caption: Having married his daughters to emperors, Michinaga became regent for his grandson. Fujiwara regency rule reached its peak.

byodoin.title: Phoenix Hall of Byodo-in Built
byodoin.caption: Fujiwara no Yorimichi turned his villa at Uji into a temple with this Amida hall, a vision of paradise on earth. It appears on the 10-yen coin.

insei.title: Cloistered Rule Begins
insei.caption: Emperor Shirakawa kept running the government after giving up the throne. Retired emperors took power from the Fujiwara regents.

hogen_no_ran.title: Hogen Rebellion
hogen_no_ran.caption: A war between Retired Emperor Sutoku and Emperor Go-Shirakawa, tangled with feuds of the Fujiwara, Minamoto and Taira. Warriors now decided politics.

heiji_no_ran.title: Heiji Rebellion
heiji_no_ran.caption: A feud among Go-Shirakawa's aides ended with Taira no Kiyomori defeating Minamoto no Yoshitomo. Yoshitomo's son Yoritomo was exiled to Izu.

kiyomori_daijo.title: Kiyomori Becomes Chancellor
kiyomori_daijo.caption: Taira no Kiyomori was the first warrior to become Grand Chancellor. His clan held so many posts that only Taira seemed to count.

dannoura.title: Battle of Dan-no-ura
dannoura.caption: Minamoto no Yoshitsune destroyed the Taira in a final sea battle in the Kanmon Strait. The child Emperor Antoku sank with the imperial regalia.

yoritomo_shogun.title: Minamoto no Yoritomo Becomes Shogun
yoritomo_shogun.caption: After Go-Shirakawa's death the court named Yoritomo shogun. The warrior government based in Kamakura took its full form.

jokyu_no_ran.title: Jokyu War
jokyu_no_ran.caption: Retired Emperor Go-Toba raised troops to overthrow the Kamakura shogunate, but lost and was exiled to Oki. The shogunate placed a deputy in Kyoto.

goseibai_shikimoku.title: Goseibai Shikimoku
goseibai_shikimoku.caption: The first law code for warriors, issued by regent Hojo Yasutoki. Its 51 articles set rules for lawsuits and became a model for later warrior law.

bunei_no_eki.title: First Mongol Invasion
bunei_no_eki.caption: A Mongol and Korean army struck Tsushima and Iki and landed at Hakata Bay. Massed tactics and exploding bombs troubled the samurai.

koan_no_eki.title: Second Mongol Invasion
koan_no_eki.caption: The Mongols came again with a huge army. Stopped by samurai and a defensive wall, they could not land, and a storm wrecked their fleet.

kamakura_metsubo.title: Fall of the Kamakura Shogunate
kamakura_metsubo.caption: Nitta Yoshisada attacked Kamakura and the Hojo took their own lives. Around the same time Ashikaga Takauji took the shogunate's Kyoto office.

kenmu_shinsei.title: Kenmu Restoration
kenmu_shinsei.caption: Emperor Go-Daigo's attempt at direct imperial rule. Rewards that favored courtiers angered the warriors, and it collapsed in about three years.

takauji_shogun.title: Ashikaga Takauji Becomes Shogun
takauji_shogun.caption: Takauji turned against Go-Daigo and was named shogun by the Northern Court emperor. He founded the Muromachi shogunate in Kyoto.

nanboku_goitsu.title: Northern and Southern Courts Reunited
nanboku_goitsu.caption: Through Ashikaga Yoshimitsu, the Southern emperor returned to Kyoto and handed over the regalia, ending some 60 years of split courts.

kinkaku.title: Golden Pavilion Built
kinkaku.caption: A gold-leafed pavilion Ashikaga Yoshimitsu built in northern Kyoto, later a Zen temple. It symbolizes the blend of court and warrior culture.

onin_no_ran.title: Onin War
onin_no_ran.caption: A shogun succession dispute, tangled with feuds among powerful lords, raged in Kyoto for 11 years. The capital was ruined and the Warring States age began.

teppo_denrai.title: Arrival of Firearms
teppo_denrai.caption: A lord on Tanegashima bought guns from Portuguese on a ship that drifted ashore. Soon mass-produced in Japan, they transformed warfare.

xavier_raichi.title: Francis Xavier Arrives
xavier_raichi.caption: The Jesuit Francis Xavier landed at Kagoshima and brought Christianity to Japan. He stayed about two years, preaching in many places.

okehazama.title: Battle of Okehazama
okehazama.caption: Oda Nobunaga of Owari killed Imagawa Yoshimoto, who led a far larger army, in a surprise attack. The little-known Nobunaga became famous overnight.

muromachi_metsubo.title: Fall of the Muromachi Shogunate
muromachi_metsubo.caption: Oda Nobunaga drove shogun Ashikaga Yoshiaki out of Kyoto. After 15 shoguns, the Muromachi shogunate effectively came to an end.

nagashino.title: Battle of Nagashino
nagashino.caption: Oda Nobunaga and Tokugawa Ieyasu defeated Takeda Katsuyori's cavalry. It is famed for its fences against horses and massed guns.

honnoji.title: Honno-ji Incident
honnoji.caption: On the verge of unifying Japan, Oda Nobunaga was attacked by his vassal Akechi Mitsuhide at Honno-ji and killed himself. Hideyoshi soon beat Mitsuhide.

katanagari.title: Sword Hunt
katanagari.caption: Toyotomi Hideyoshi ordered farmers to give up swords and guns. It prevented uprisings and drew a line between warriors and farmers.

tenka_toitsu.title: Hideyoshi Unifies Japan
tenka_toitsu.caption: Toyotomi Hideyoshi destroyed the Hojo of Odawara and won over the lords of the northeast. The long civil wars finally paused.

bunroku_no_eki.title: First Invasion of Korea
bunroku_no_eki.caption: Hideyoshi sent a huge army to Korea, aiming to conquer Ming China. It reached Seoul, but suffered against Yi Sun-sin's navy and Ming troops.

sekigahara.title: Battle of Sekigahara
sekigahara.caption: Tokugawa Ieyasu's Eastern Army met Ishida Mitsunari's Western Army in the battle for the realm. A key defection let the East win in a day.

edo_bakufu.title: Edo Shogunate Founded
edo_bakufu.caption: Tokugawa Ieyasu was named shogun and set up his government in Edo. The Tokugawa would rule Japan for more than 260 years.

osaka_natsu.title: Summer Siege of Osaka
osaka_natsu.caption: Tokugawa forces attacked Osaka Castle again. Toyotomi Hideyori and his mother died, ending the clan. Sanada Nobushige's stand is famous.

shimabara.title: Shimabara Rebellion
shimabara.caption: People of Shimabara and Amakusa, crushed by taxes and persecution of Christians, held Hara Castle under Amakusa Shiro. It was put down the next year.

sakoku.title: Portuguese Ships Banned
sakoku.caption: Fearing the spread of Christianity, the shogunate barred Portuguese ships. This sealed the policy of national isolation known as sakoku.

kyoho_kaikaku.title: Kyoho Reforms
kyoho_kaikaku.caption: Reforms by the eighth shogun, Tokugawa Yoshimune. Thrift, new rice fields and a public petition box aimed to fix the shogunate's finances.

kaitai_shinsho.title: Kaitai Shinsho Published
kaitai_shinsho.caption: Sugita Genpaku, Maeno Ryotaku and others painstakingly translated a Dutch anatomy book. It sparked the spread of Dutch learning.

kansei_kaikaku.title: Kansei Reforms
kansei_kaikaku.caption: Reforms by senior councilor Matsudaira Sadanobu. He pushed thrift and village recovery and banned non-official teachings, but his strictness was disliked.

ino_sokuryo.title: Ino Tadataka Begins His Survey
ino_sokuryo.caption: After studying astronomy past age 50, Tadataka set out to survey Ezo. Pacing step by step, he went on to map the whole country.

oshio_no_ran.title: Oshio Heihachiro's Rebellion
oshio_no_ran.caption: A former Osaka police official rose up to help people starving in the Tenpo famine. Crushed in half a day, it still shocked the shogunate.

perry_raiko.title: Perry Arrives
perry_raiko.caption: America's Commodore Perry appeared at Uraga with four warships, demanding that Japan open up. The shock of the "Black Ships" began years of upheaval.

nichibei_washin.title: Convention of Kanagawa
nichibei_washin.caption: A treaty signed on Perry's return. It opened Shimoda and Hakodate and let American ships get water and food, ending isolation.

nichibei_shuko.title: Harris Treaty
nichibei_shuko.caption: Chief minister Ii Naosuke signed this trade treaty without imperial approval. It was unequal, granting extraterritoriality and denying Japan tariff control.

sakuradamon.title: Sakuradamon Incident
sakuradamon.caption: Chief minister Ii Naosuke was assassinated by Mito ronin outside Edo Castle's Sakurada Gate. The shogunate's authority was badly shaken.

taisei_houkan.title: Return of Power to the Emperor
taisei_houkan.caption: The 15th shogun, Tokugawa Yoshinobu, offered to return political power to the court. Over 260 years of Edo shogunate rule came to an end.

boshin_senso.title: Boshin War
boshin_senso.caption: A civil war between the new government and shogunate forces, starting at Toba-Fushimi. It ended at Hakodate the next year, securing the new regime.

haihan_chiken.title: Domains Replaced by Prefectures
haihan_chiken.caption: The Meiji government abolished the domains and set up prefectures run by officials from the center. Rule by lords ended.

seinan_senso.title: Satsuma Rebellion
seinan_senso.caption: Former samurai of Kagoshima rose under Saigo Takamori in the last and largest samurai revolt. Beaten by a conscript army, Saigo took his life.

teikoku_kenpo.title: Meiji Constitution
teikoku_kenpo.caption: Drafted by Ito Hirobumi and others on a German model and granted by the emperor to the people. It was East Asia's first modern constitution.

nisshin_senso.title: First Sino-Japanese War
nisshin_senso.caption: Japan and Qing China fought over control of Korea. Japan won and, by the Treaty of Shimonoseki, gained an indemnity and Taiwan.

nichiro_senso.title: Russo-Japanese War
nichiro_senso.caption: Japan and Russia fought over Manchuria and Korea. Japan won at Port Arthur and the Sea of Japan, but both sides were too drained to go on.

kanto_daishinsai.title: Great Kanto Earthquake
kanto_daishinsai.caption: A huge quake struck southern Kanto just before noon on September 1. Fires burned Tokyo and Yokohama, and over 100,000 died or went missing.

futsu_senkyo.title: Universal Male Suffrage Law
futsu_senkyo.caption: It dropped the tax requirement, giving the vote to all men 25 and over. The Peace Preservation Law came with it. Women still could not vote.

niniroku.title: February 26 Incident
niniroku.caption: Young army officers led about 1,400 soldiers in attacks on the prime minister's residence and killed Takahashi Korekiyo and others. The military grew stronger.

taiheiyo_senso.title: Pacific War Begins
taiheiyo_senso.caption: On December 8, Japan attacked Pearl Harbor in Hawaii and the Malay Peninsula, starting war with the United States and Britain.

shusen.title: End of the War
shusen.caption: Japan accepted the Potsdam Declaration, and on August 15 Emperor Showa announced defeat by radio, just after the atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

kenpo_shiko.title: Constitution of Japan Takes Effect
kenpo_shiko.caption: In force from May 3. Its pillars are popular sovereignty, basic human rights and pacifism. The day is still Constitution Day.

sanfrancisco.title: Treaty of San Francisco
sanfrancisco.caption: Signed by Prime Minister Yoshida Shigeru. When it took effect the next year, Japan regained independence. The US-Japan Security Treaty was signed the same day.

shinkansen.title: Tokaido Shinkansen Opens
shinkansen.caption: The world's first high-speed railway, linking Tokyo and Shin-Osaka. Opened just before the Tokyo Olympics, it symbolized rapid growth.

tokyo_olympic_1964.title: Tokyo Olympics (Asia's First)
tokyo_olympic_1964.caption: The first Olympics held in Asia showed the world Japan's postwar recovery. The women's volleyball team, the "Witches of the Orient," won gold.

osaka_banpaku.title: Expo '70 in Osaka (Asia's First)
osaka_banpaku.caption: Asia's first world's fair, held in the Senri Hills of Osaka. Okamoto Taro's Tower of the Sun stood there, and over 64 million people came.

okinawa_henkan.title: Return of Okinawa
okinawa_henkan.caption: Okinawa, under US administration, came back to Japan under the Sato Eisaku cabinet, though huge US military bases remained.

hanshin_awaji.title: Great Hanshin Earthquake
hanshin_awaji.caption: A major quake struck southern Hyogo early on January 17. Over 6,000 died, mostly around Kobe. It is called the first year of volunteering.

nagano_olympic.title: Nagano Winter Olympics
nagano_olympic.caption: Winter Olympics held in Nagano. Gold in the team ski jump and other wins thrilled the whole country.

higashi_nihon.title: Great East Japan Earthquake
higashi_nihon.caption: A giant quake and tsunami off Sanriku on March 11 devastated the Tohoku coast and caused the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear accident.

kin_in.title: King of Na Receives a Gold Seal
kin_in.caption: The king of Na in Kyushu sent envoys to the Later Han and received a seal from Emperor Guangwu. A gold seal found on Shikanoshima is thought to be it.

kentoshi_first.title: First Envoys to Tang China
kentoshi_first.caption: Inukami no Mitasuki led the first mission to Tang. For some 200 years, students and monks brought continental culture back to Japan.

yoritomo_kyohei.title: Minamoto no Yoritomo Rises
yoritomo_kyohei.caption: Answering Prince Mochihito's call, the exiled Yoritomo raised troops in Izu. Beaten at Ishibashiyama, he rallied the warriors of Kanto.

einin_tokusei.title: Einin Debt-Relief Edict
einin_tokusei.caption: To save struggling retainers, the Kamakura shogunate let them reclaim land they had sold for free. It threw the economy into confusion.

kango_boeki.title: Tally Trade Begins
kango_boeki.caption: Ashikaga Yoshimitsu began trade with Ming China, using tally slips to tell envoys from pirates. Copper coins and raw silk flowed into Japan.

kaga_ikko.title: Kaga Ikko Uprising
kaga_ikko.caption: Followers of True Pure Land Buddhism overthrew the governor of Kaga and ruled it themselves for about 100 years, a "province held by farmers."

sankin_kotai.title: Alternate Attendance System
sankin_kotai.caption: Set by the third shogun, Tokugawa Iemitsu. Lords had to live in Edo every other year, and their wives and children had to stay there.

dejima.title: Dutch Trading Post Moved to Dejima
dejima.caption: The Dutch post at Hirado was moved to Dejima, a man-made island in Nagasaki. It remained Japan's window on the West.

meireki_taika.title: Great Fire of Meireki
meireki_taika.caption: A fire burned most of Edo, including the castle keep. Over 100,000 may have died. The city was rebuilt with firebreaks.

hoei_funka.title: Hoei Eruption of Mount Fuji
hoei_funka.caption: Mount Fuji's last major eruption, 49 days after the Hoei earthquake. Volcanic ash fell even on the streets of Edo.

tenpo_kaikaku.title: Tenpo Reforms
tenpo_kaikaku.caption: Reforms by senior councilor Mizuno Tadakuni. He broke up merchant guilds and pushed thrift, but a land order met resistance and the reforms failed.

tetsudo_kaigyo.title: First Railway Opens
tetsudo_kaigyo.caption: Japan's first railway, built with British technology. Steam trains linked Shinbashi and Yokohama in about an hour.

naikaku_seido.title: Cabinet System Created
naikaku_seido.caption: The old council of state was replaced by a modern cabinet system. Ito Hirobumi became the first prime minister.

nichiei_domei.title: Anglo-Japanese Alliance
nichiei_domei.caption: An alliance between Japan and Britain, both wary of Russian expansion. Backed by it, Japan went on to fight the Russo-Japanese War.

kokuren_kamei.title: Japan Joins the United Nations
kokuren_kamei.caption: After the Soviet-Japanese joint declaration ended Soviet objections, Japan was admitted to the UN and returned to the world community.

wado_kaichin.title: Wado Kaichin Coins Minted
wado_kaichin.caption: Coins made after copper was presented from Musashi. Modeled on Tang coins, they also helped pay for building Heijo-kyo.

sanze_isshin.title: Law of Three Generations
sanze_isshin.caption: Land cleared with new irrigation could be held for three generations. It aimed to increase farmland, but had little effect.

kokubunji.title: Edict on Provincial Temples
kokubunji.caption: Emperor Shomu ordered a temple built in every province, hoping Buddhism would protect the state from epidemics and revolts.

otenmon.title: Otenmon Incident
otenmon.caption: The Otenmon gate of the palace was set on fire, and the noble Tomo no Yoshio was exiled as the culprit. Fujiwara no Yoshifusa tightened his grip on power.

konjikido.title: Konjikido of Chuson-ji Built
konjikido.caption: An Amida hall covered in gold leaf, built at Hiraizumi by Fujiwara no Kiyohira. It preserves the Pure Land culture that bloomed in the north.

jodoshu.title: Honen Founds Pure Land Buddhism
jodoshu.caption: Honen taught that anyone could reach paradise by chanting the nembutsu. His teaching spread from nobles to commoners.

kongo_rikishi.title: Guardian Kings of Todai-ji's South Gate
kongo_rikishi.caption: Wooden statues over 8 meters tall, made by Unkei, Kaikei and others in about 70 days. Their powerful realism defines Kamakura sculpture.

dogen_soto.title: Dogen Brings Soto Zen
dogen_soto.caption: Dogen returned from Song China and taught Soto Zen, centered on simply sitting in meditation. He later founded Eihei-ji in Echizen.

nichiren.title: Nichiren Founds His Sect
nichiren.caption: Nichiren taught chanting the title of the Lotus Sutra. He harshly attacked other sects and kept preaching despite exile by the shogunate.

kenmu_shikimoku.title: Kenmu Code
kenmu_shikimoku.caption: Ashikaga Takauji's statement of policy for a new warrior government. Some date the founding of the Muromachi shogunate from it.

ryukyu_okoku.title: Ryukyu Kingdom Founded
ryukyu_okoku.caption: Sho Hashi unified Okinawa Island, then split into three kingdoms. Rich from relay trade, the kingdom ruled from Shuri for over 400 years.

nobunaga_joraku.title: Oda Nobunaga Enters Kyoto
nobunaga_joraku.caption: Backing Ashikaga Yoshiaki, Nobunaga marched into Kyoto and made him the 15th shogun. His drive to unify Japan began in earnest.

hieizan.title: Burning of Mount Hiei
hieizan.caption: Nobunaga's army attacked and burned Enryaku-ji, which had aided his enemies. Monks and townspeople were killed, shocking the Buddhist world.

azuchi.title: Azuchi Castle Begun
azuchi.caption: Nobunaga's castle on the east shore of Lake Biwa, with a towering keep. Free markets in its town made trade and crafts thrive.

tensho_shisetsu.title: Tensho Embassy to Europe
tensho_shisetsu.caption: Christian lords of Kyushu sent four boys to Rome. Planned by Valignano, the group was received by the Pope.

bateren_tsuiho.title: Edict Expelling Missionaries
bateren_tsuiho.caption: Right after conquering Kyushu, Hideyoshi ordered missionaries to leave Japan. Since trade with Europeans went on, it was not strictly enforced.

keicho_no_eki.title: Second Invasion of Korea
keicho_no_eki.caption: Hideyoshi sent troops to Korea again. The fighting went badly, and when Hideyoshi died the next year the Japanese army withdrew.

ryukyu_shinko.title: Satsuma Invades Ryukyu
ryukyu_shinko.caption: The Shimazu of Satsuma invaded Ryukyu, took Shuri Castle and brought it under their control. Ryukyu kept ties with Ming as well.

keicho_shisetsu.title: Keicho Embassy to Europe
keicho_shisetsu.caption: Date Masamune of Sendai sent Hasekura Tsunenaga to Spain and Rome. They crossed the Pacific, but the trade talks failed.

buke_shohatto.title: Laws for Military Houses
buke_shohatto.caption: Issued right after the Osaka sieges to control the lords. Repairing castles or arranging marriages without permission was banned.

sonezaki.title: Love Suicides at Sonezaki Premieres
sonezaki.caption: A puppet play by Chikamatsu Monzaemon based on a real double suicide. Its tale of townsfolk in love was a huge hit.

tanuma.title: Tanuma Okitsugu Takes Power
tanuma.caption: A senior councilor who favored commerce, taxing merchant guilds and draining marshes. Bribery spread, and he fell after the Tenmei famine.

asama_funka.title: Tenmei Eruption of Mount Asama
asama_funka.caption: Pyroclastic flows buried villages and floods followed, killing many. The eruption worsened the Tenmei famine.

laxman.title: Laxman Arrives at Nemuro
laxman.caption: Russian envoy Adam Laxman came to Nemuro with castaway Daikokuya Kodayu, seeking trade. The shogunate gave him a permit to enter Nagasaki.

rezanov.title: Rezanov Arrives at Nagasaki
rezanov.caption: Russian envoy Rezanov came with the permit, but was kept waiting half a year and refused trade. Russian raids on Sakhalin followed.

phaeton.title: Phaeton Incident
phaeton.caption: A British warship chasing Dutch ships entered Nagasaki, seized supplies and left. The Nagasaki magistrate took responsibility by killing himself.

siebold.title: Siebold Arrives
siebold.caption: The German doctor Siebold came as physician to the Dutch post. At his Narutaki school in Nagasaki he taught Western medicine to Takano Choei and others.

bansha.title: Bansha no Goku Purge
bansha.caption: Scholars of Dutch learning such as Watanabe Kazan and Takano Choei were punished for criticizing the shogunate's isolation policy.

satsuei.title: Anglo-Satsuma War
satsuei.caption: To avenge the Namamugi Incident, a British fleet shelled Kagoshima. Satsuma saw that expelling foreigners was hopeless and drew closer to Britain.

kinmon.title: Kinmon Incident
kinmon.caption: Choshu, driven out of Kyoto, marched on the imperial palace and was beaten by Satsuma and Aizu. It is also called the Hamaguri Gate Rebellion.

satcho_domei.title: Satsuma-Choshu Alliance
satcho_domei.caption: Brokered by Sakamoto Ryoma and others, rivals Satsuma and Choshu joined hands. It set off the drive to overthrow the shogunate.

gokajo.title: Charter Oath
gokajo.caption: The new government's goals, sworn by Emperor Meiji before the gods. It promised to convene assemblies and value public opinion.

hanseki_hokan.title: Return of Land and People
hanseki_hokan.caption: The lords gave their land and people back to the emperor. They stayed on as governors, a step toward abolishing the domains.

chiso_kaisei.title: Land Tax Reform
chiso_kaisei.caption: Rice taxes were replaced by a cash tax of 3% of land value. Government finances stabilized, but farmer uprisings followed.

minsen_giin.title: Petition for an Elected Assembly
minsen_giin.caption: Itagaki Taisuke and others urged the government to open an assembly chosen by the people. The Freedom and People's Rights Movement began here.

nicchoshuko.title: Japan-Korea Treaty of 1876
nicchoshuko.caption: Imposed on Korea after the Ganghwa Island incident. It opened Korea to Japan on terms unequal for Korea.

kokkai_kaisetsu.title: Edict Promising a National Diet
kokkai_kaisetsu.caption: Emperor Meiji promised to open a parliament in ten years, in response to criticism raised by a scandal over the sale of government property.

shimonoseki.title: Treaty of Shimonoseki
shimonoseki.caption: The treaty ending the First Sino-Japanese War. Qing recognized Korean independence and gave Japan Liaodong, Taiwan and an indemnity.

yawata.title: Yawata Steel Works Opens
yawata.caption: A state steelworks in Fukuoka, built partly with the war indemnity from Qing. Japan's heavy industry started here.

portsmouth.title: Treaty of Portsmouth
portsmouth.caption: Peace treaty ending the Russo-Japanese War, brokered by the United States. Anger at getting no indemnity set off the Hibiya riots in Tokyo.

kanzei_jishuken.title: Tariff Autonomy Restored
kanzei_jishuken.caption: Foreign Minister Komura Jutaro won full control over tariffs from the US and others, completing revision of the unequal treaties.

kome_sodo.title: Rice Riots Spread Nationwide
kome_sodo.caption: Hoarding drove rice prices sky-high, and protests begun by fishing village wives in Toyama spread nationwide. The Terauchi cabinet fell.

hara_naikaku.title: Hara Takashi Forms a Cabinet
hara_naikaku.caption: After the rice riots, party leader Hara formed the first true party cabinet. Holding no title, he was called the "commoner prime minister."

radio_hoso.title: Radio Broadcasting Begins
radio_hoso.caption: The Tokyo Broadcasting Station went on the air. The next year the stations merged into NHK, the Japan Broadcasting Corporation.

manshu_jihen.title: Manchurian Incident
manshu_jihen.caption: The Kwantung Army blew up the South Manchuria Railway at Liutiaohu, blamed China and attacked. Manchukuo was set up the next year.

renmei_dattai.title: Japan Leaves the League of Nations
renmei_dattai.caption: A report refusing to recognize Manchukuo passed, and envoy Matsuoka walked out. Japan left the League and grew more isolated.

nicchu_senso.title: Second Sino-Japanese War Begins
nicchu_senso.caption: A clash at the Marco Polo Bridge near Beijing set off full-scale war with China. It dragged on and led into the Pacific War.

yukawa.title: Yukawa Hideki Wins the Nobel Prize
yukawa.caption: Yukawa, who predicted the meson in theory, became the first Japanese Nobel laureate, giving great hope to postwar Japan.

nicchu_kokko.title: Japan-China Relations Normalized
nicchu_kokko.caption: Prime Minister Tanaka Kakuei visited Beijing and opened relations with the People's Republic. China sent two pandas to Japan.

skytree.title: Tokyo Skytree Opens
skytree.caption: A 634-meter broadcasting tower in Sumida, Tokyo. It is the world's tallest freestanding tower.

fujiwara_kyo.title: Capital Moved to Fujiwara-kyo
fujiwara_kyo.caption: Empress Jito's new capital north of Asuka, the first true Japanese capital with grid streets. It served until the move to Heijo-kyo in 710.

oshikatsu.title: Rebellion of Emi no Oshikatsu
oshikatsu.caption: Strongman Emi no Oshikatsu (Fujiwara no Nakamaro) rose against Retired Empress Koken and the monk Dokyo, but was defeated and killed in Omi.

dokyo.title: Usa Hachiman Oracle Incident
dokyo.caption: An oracle said the monk Dokyo should take the throne, but Wake no Kiyomaro reported it false. Dokyo's ambitions ended with Empress Shotoku's death.

nagaokakyo.title: Capital Moved to Nagaoka-kyo
nagaokakyo.caption: Emperor Kanmu left Heijo-kyo for this capital. After the murder of its builder Fujiwara no Tanetsugu, it was abandoned for Heian-kyo in ten years.

tamuramaro.title: Sakanoue no Tamuramaro Made Shogun
tamuramaro.caption: Appointed by Emperor Kanmu to subdue the Emishi, he took the Isawa region and made the chief Aterui surrender.

kukai_saicho.title: Saicho and Kukai Go to Tang
kukai_saicho.caption: Saicho and Kukai sailed to Tang with an envoy mission. Back home they founded the Tendai and Shingon sects, the base of Heian Buddhism.

kanpaku_mototsune.title: Fujiwara no Mototsune Becomes Kanpaku
kanpaku_mototsune.caption: By Emperor Uda's edict, Mototsune became the first official kanpaku. In a later dispute the Fujiwara showed their power even over the emperor.

michizane_sasen.title: Sugawara no Michizane Exiled
michizane_sasen.caption: Minister Michizane was slandered by Fujiwara no Tokihira and sent to Dazaifu. He died two years later and came to be worshiped as a god of learning.

toi_nyuko.title: Toi Invasion
toi_nyuko.caption: Pirates thought to be Jurchen raided Tsushima, Iki and northern Kyushu. Fujiwara no Takaie of Dazaifu led local warriors to drive them off.

shinkokin.title: Shin Kokin Wakashu Compiled
shinkokin.caption: An imperial anthology compiled by Fujiwara no Teika and others for Retired Emperor Go-Toba. It is known for its delicate, suggestive style.

hojoki.title: Hojoki Written
hojoki.caption: An essay by Kamo no Chomei. It begins "The flowing river never stops" and tells of disasters and the impermanence of the world.

sanetomo.title: Assassination of Minamoto no Sanetomo
sanetomo.caption: The third shogun was killed by his nephew Kugyo at Tsurugaoka Hachimangu. The Minamoto line ended and the Hojo regents took firm control.

genko.title: Genko Incident
genko.caption: Emperor Go-Daigo again plotted to overthrow the shogunate, failed and was exiled to Oki. But Kusunoki Masashige and others kept fighting.

hana_no_gosho.title: Palace of Flowers Built
hana_no_gosho.caption: The third shogun, Ashikaga Yoshimitsu, built this mansion in Muromachi, Kyoto. It gave the shogunate its name and became the center of government.

oei_no_ran.title: Oei Rebellion
oei_no_ran.caption: The powerful lord Ouchi Yoshihiro rebelled against Ashikaga Yoshimitsu at Sakai but was killed. The shogun's power grew even stronger.

edojo_chikujo.title: Ota Dokan Builds Edo Castle
edojo_chikujo.caption: Ota Dokan, a retainer of the Uesugi, built a castle at Edo. Tokugawa Ieyasu later moved in, and it became the shogunate's home.

itsukushima.title: Battle of Itsukushima
itsukushima.caption: Mori Motonari lured Sue Harukata's large army onto narrow Itsukushima and crushed it by surprise, a first step to ruling western Honshu.

kawanakajima.title: Fourth Battle of Kawanakajima
kawanakajima.caption: The fiercest of the clashes between Takeda Shingen and Uesugi Kenshin in Shinano. Losses were heavy, and Shingen's brother Nobushige fell.

anegawa.title: Battle of Anegawa
anegawa.caption: Oda and Tokugawa forces beat the Azai and Asakura at the Ane River in Omi, leading to the later fall of both clans.

ishiyama.title: End of the Ishiyama War
ishiyama.caption: An imperial truce ended Nobunaga's 11-year war with the Honganji sect. Its leader Kennyo left Ishiyama in Osaka.

shizugatake.title: Battle of Shizugatake
shizugatake.caption: Hashiba Hideyoshi defeated Shibata Katsuie in Omi and secured his place as Nobunaga's successor. His star warriors were hailed as the Seven Spears.

komaki.title: Battle of Komaki and Nagakute
komaki.caption: Hideyoshi fought Tokugawa Ieyasu and Oda Nobukatsu. Ieyasu won in the field, but Hideyoshi made peace with Nobukatsu and ended the war.

nijuroku_seijin.title: Martyrdom of the 26 Saints
nijuroku_seijin.caption: On Hideyoshi's order, 26 missionaries and Japanese Christians were executed at Nishizaka in Nagasaki. The Pope later made them saints.

tsushinshi.title: First Korean Embassy to Edo
tsushinshi.caption: After the invasions of Korea, Korean envoys came to Edo to restore relations. They visited 12 times during the Edo period.

keian.title: Keian Uprising
keian.caption: Military scholar Yui Shosetsu plotted to overthrow the shogunate with masterless samurai, but was betrayed. It showed that ronin were a social problem.

shakushain.title: Shakushain's Revolt
shakushain.caption: The Ainu chief Shakushain rose against the Matsumae domain's unfair trading, but was killed at peace talks.

okuno_hosomichi.title: Basho's Narrow Road to the Deep North
okuno_hosomichi.caption: Matsuo Basho left Edo with his disciple Sora to tour the northeast and the Hokuriku. Some of his most famous haiku come from this journey.

kojikiden.title: Motoori Norinaga Completes Kojiki-den
kojikiden.caption: Norinaga's commentary on the Kojiki, 35 years in the making. It perfected kokugaku, the study of Japan's native spirit.

enkai_yochi.title: Ino's Map of Japan Completed
enkai_yochi.caption: A map of Japan finished by Ino Tadataka's disciples after his death. Its surveyed precision amazed Westerners in the 1860s.

ansei_jishin.title: Ansei Edo Earthquake
ansei_jishin.caption: A great quake struck right under Edo. Fires burned the city and Fujita Toko of Mito died. Catfish prints meant to calm quakes became popular.

ansei_taigoku.title: Ansei Purge
ansei_taigoku.caption: Chief minister Ii Naosuke crushed opponents of the treaties and of his choice of shogun. Yoshida Shoin, Hashimoto Sanai and others were executed.

kanrin_maru.title: Kanrin Maru Crosses the Pacific
kanrin_maru.caption: A shogunate warship carrying Katsu Kaishu sailed to San Francisco, said to be the first Pacific crossing by a Japanese-crewed ship. Fukuzawa Yukichi was aboard.

namamugi.title: Namamugi Incident
namamugi.caption: Britons who crossed a Satsuma lord's procession were cut down by his samurai. It led to the Anglo-Satsuma War the next year.

iwakura.title: Iwakura Mission Departs
iwakura.caption: Iwakura Tomomi led Okubo Toshimichi, Kido Takayoshi and others to the US and Europe. Treaty talks failed, but they studied modern nations.

tomioka.title: Tomioka Silk Mill Opens
tomioka.caption: A state model factory in Gunma using French technology. Young women from across Japan learned silk reeling there. It is a World Heritage Site.

okinawa_ken.title: Okinawa Prefecture Created
okinawa_ken.caption: The Meiji government abolished the Ryukyu domain, sent troops and set up Okinawa Prefecture. The Ryukyu Kingdom came to an end.

rokumeikan.title: Rokumeikan Opens
rokumeikan.caption: A Western-style hall built by Inoue Kaoru to help revise the treaties. A symbol of Westernization, it hosted balls for foreign guests.

teikoku_gikai.title: First Imperial Diet
teikoku_gikai.caption: The first parliament under the Meiji Constitution. Only men paying 15 yen or more in direct taxes could vote for the lower house.

otsu.title: Otsu Incident
otsu.caption: The visiting Russian crown prince was slashed by a police guard in Shiga. Chief Justice Kojima Iken upheld the independence of the courts.

nijuikkajo.title: Twenty-One Demands
nijuikkajo.caption: During World War I, Japan pressed China for more rights. China marked the day it accepted as a day of national shame, fueling anti-Japanese protests.

renmei_kamei.title: Japan Joins the League of Nations
renmei_kamei.caption: Japan joined the new League after World War I as a permanent member of its council. Nitobe Inazo served as an under-secretary-general.

goichigo.title: May 15 Incident
goichigo.caption: Young naval officers stormed the prime minister's residence and shot Prime Minister Inukai Tsuyoshi. The era of party cabinets ended.

sangoku_domei.title: Tripartite Pact
sangoku_domei.caption: A military alliance of Japan, Germany and Italy signed in Berlin. It sealed Japan's rift with the United States.

kenpo_kofu.title: Constitution of Japan Promulgated
kenpo_kofu.caption: Promulgated on November 3, based on a GHQ draft and debated in the Diet. The day is now Culture Day.

terebi.title: TV Broadcasting Begins
terebi.caption: NHK and Nippon TV began regular broadcasts. Crowds gathered at street TVs to watch pro wrestling, and soon sets spread into homes.

anpo.title: US-Japan Security Treaty Revised
anpo.caption: The Kishi Nobusuke cabinet signed a new security treaty. Massive protests surrounded the Diet, and the cabinet resigned.

kawabata.title: Kawabata Yasunari Wins the Nobel Prize
kawabata.caption: The author of Snow Country became Japan's first Nobel laureate in literature. His lecture was titled "Japan, the Beautiful and Myself."

narita.title: Narita Airport Opens
narita.caption: New Tokyo International Airport in Chiba opened after fierce local opposition, 12 years after it was planned.

seikan.title: Seikan Tunnel Opens
seikan.caption: An undersea tunnel linking Honshu and Hokkaido, about 54 km long. A deadly ferry disaster had spurred its construction.

aichi_banpaku.title: Expo 2005 Aichi
aichi_banpaku.caption: A world's fair in Aichi on the theme "Nature's Wisdom." Nicknamed "Love the Earth," its mascots Morizo and Kiccoro were a hit.

iwai.title: Iwai Rebellion
iwai.caption: Iwai, a chieftain of Tsukushi, rebelled to block Yamato troops bound for Korea. He was put down by Mononobe no Arakabi the next year.

teibi.title: Teibi War
teibi.caption: Soga no Umako and Mononobe no Moriya fought over Buddhism, and the Soga destroyed the Mononobe. Prince Umayado is said to have joined the Soga.

asukadera.title: Asuka-dera Begun
asukadera.caption: Japan's first full-scale temple, begun by Soga no Umako. Builders came from Baekje, and the Asuka Great Buddha was enshrined there.

nagaya_no_o.title: Prince Nagaya Incident
nagaya_no_o.caption: Minister Prince Nagaya, accused of treason, killed himself. It is seen as a plot by the four Fujiwara brothers to seize power.

hirotsugu.title: Fujiwara no Hirotsugu Rebellion
hirotsugu.caption: Hirotsugu, sent away to Dazaifu, raised troops in Kyushu demanding the removal of Kibi no Makibi and others. After it, Emperor Shomu kept moving the capital.

isawajo.title: Isawa Castle Built
isawajo.caption: A fort built by Sakanoue no Tamuramaro in Emishi lands. The northern military headquarters moved there from Taga Castle.

kusuko.title: Kusuko Incident
kusuko.caption: Fujiwara no Kusuko and her allies lost a struggle between Retired Emperor Heizei and Emperor Saga. Saga set up a private secretariat to guard secrets.

heike_nokyo.title: Heike Nokyo Dedicated
heike_nokyo.caption: Lavish sutras that Taira no Kiyomori offered to Itsukushima Shrine for his clan's prosperity. Adorned in gold and silver, they are a peak of Heian craft.

shishigatani.title: Shishigatani Plot
shishigatani.caption: Aides of Go-Shirakawa plotted against the Taira at Shishigatani in Kyoto, but were betrayed. Shunkan and others were exiled to an island.

fukuhara.title: Capital Moved to Fukuhara
fukuhara.caption: Taira no Kiyomori tried to move the capital to Fukuhara, near his base for trade with Song China. Opposition was strong, and it returned to Kyoto in half a year.

kurikara.title: Battle of Kurikara Pass
kurikara.caption: Minamoto no Yoshinaka crushed a large Taira army on the Kaga-Etchu border, said to have used oxen with torches on their horns. He then marched on Kyoto.

ichinotani.title: Battle of Ichi-no-Tani
ichinotani.caption: Minamoto no Yoshitsune is said to have charged down a cliff to break the Taira camp. The death of young Taira no Atsumori is told of this battle.

yashima.title: Battle of Yashima
yashima.caption: Yoshitsune crossed to Shikoku in a storm and struck the Taira from behind. It is famous for Nasu no Yoichi shooting a fan from a boat.

oshu_fujiwara.title: Fall of the Oshu Fujiwara
oshu_fujiwara.caption: Yoritomo sent a great army to destroy the Fujiwara of Hiraizumi for sheltering Yoshitsune. With Yasuhira killed, his rule covered all Japan.

kamakura_daibutsu.title: Kamakura Great Buddha Cast
kamakura_daibutsu.caption: The bronze seated Amida of Kotoku-in. It once stood inside a hall, but the building was lost and the Buddha now sits in the open air.

shochu.title: Shochu Incident
shochu.caption: Emperor Go-Daigo's first plot against the shogunate leaked, and his aide Hino Suketomo was exiled to Sado. The emperor did not give up.

minatogawa.title: Battle of Minatogawa
minatogawa.caption: Kusunoki Masashige met Ashikaga Takauji's army marching from Kyushu. Defeated, he killed himself and was later revered as a loyal hero.

shocho_ikki.title: Shocho Uprising
shocho_ikki.caption: Starting with packhorse drivers in Omi, farmers around Kyoto attacked moneylenders to cancel their debts. It is called Japan's first major peasant uprising.

kakitsu.title: Kakitsu Incident
kakitsu.caption: Akamatsu Mitsusuke, governor of Harima, killed the sixth shogun Ashikaga Yoshinori at a banquet in his home. The shogun's authority was badly shaken.

ginkaku.title: Silver Pavilion Raised
ginkaku.caption: The Kannon hall of the mountain villa built by the eighth shogun Ashikaga Yoshimasa. It represents the quiet, refined Higashiyama culture.

gifu.title: Nobunaga Takes Inabayama Castle
gifu.caption: Nobunaga beat Saito Tatsuoki of Mino and took his castle. He renamed the place Gifu and began using a seal meaning "rule the realm by arms."

rikyu.title: Sen no Rikyu's Suicide
rikyu.caption: Rikyu, master of the wabi tea ceremony, angered Hideyoshi and was ordered to kill himself. The reason is still unclear.

liefde.title: The Liefde Drifts Ashore
liefde.caption: A Dutch ship drifted to Bungo. Its navigator William Adams became a trusted adviser to Tokugawa Ieyasu under the name Miura Anjin.

osaka_fuyu.title: Winter Siege of Osaka
osaka_fuyu.caption: Using a temple bell's inscription as a pretext, Ieyasu attacked Osaka Castle. After fighting at the Sanada fort, a truce filled in the castle moats.

toshogu.title: Nikko Toshogu Shrine Built
toshogu.caption: A shrine to Tokugawa Ieyasu's spirit, lavishly rebuilt by the third shogun Iemitsu. Its Yomeimon gate and three wise monkeys are famous.

saikaku.title: The Life of an Amorous Man Published
saikaku.caption: Ihara Saikaku's first popular novel, published in Osaka. Vividly showing townsfolk's desires and lives, it was part of Genroku culture.

nishikie.title: Birth of Nishiki-e Prints
nishikie.caption: Suzuki Harunobu and others began multicolor ukiyo-e prints. These bright prints spread as art that ordinary people could enjoy.

hizakurige.title: Hizakurige Published
hizakurige.caption: A comic novel by Jippensha Ikku. The misadventures of Yaji and Kita on the Tokaido were a huge hit and made townsfolk long to travel.

hakkenden.title: Hakkenden Begins Publication
hakkenden.caption: Kyokutei Bakin's epic novel, 28 years in the writing, about eight dog warriors with eight jewels. Going blind, Bakin dictated the end.

siebold_jiken.title: Siebold Incident
siebold_jiken.caption: Banned maps of Japan were found in Siebold's luggage as he was leaving. He was expelled, and the astronomer Takahashi Kageyasu died in prison.

tekijuku.title: Tekijuku School Opens
tekijuku.caption: Ogata Koan's school of Dutch learning in Osaka. It produced many future leaders, such as Fukuzawa Yukichi and Omura Masujiro.

yokohama_kaiko.title: Port of Yokohama Opens
yokohama_kaiko.caption: Yokohama opened under the Harris Treaty. A small fishing village became an international port thriving on silk exports.

shimonoseki_hogeki.title: Bombardment of Shimonoseki
shimonoseki_hogeki.caption: Fleets from Britain, France, the Netherlands and the US struck back at Choshu for firing on foreign ships. Its forts taken, Choshu gave up expelling foreigners.

edo_kaijo.title: Bloodless Surrender of Edo Castle
edo_kaijo.caption: After talks between Saigo Takamori and Katsu Kaishu, Edo Castle was handed over without a fight. The city of Edo was spared.

hakodate.title: End of the Battle of Hakodate
hakodate.caption: Enomoto Takeaki's shogunate forces held out at Goryokaku but surrendered. Hijikata Toshizo fell, and the Boshin War was over.

choheirei.title: Conscription Ordinance
choheirei.caption: All men aged 20 were made liable for military service, building a national army in place of the samurai. "Blood tax" riots opposed it.

todai.title: University of Tokyo Founded
todai.caption: Japan's first modern university, formed by merging two government schools. It later became the Imperial University.

nichigin.title: Bank of Japan Founded
nichigin.caption: Founded as the central bank under Matsukata Masayoshi. It alone issued banknotes and worked to stabilize the currency.

normanton.title: Normanton Incident
normanton.caption: A British ship sank off Kii, and all its Japanese passengers died. The captain's light sentence fed calls to revise the unequal treaties.

kyoiku_chokugo.title: Imperial Rescript on Education
kyoiku_chokugo.caption: Educational principles of loyalty and patriotism, issued in the emperor's words. Read aloud in prewar schools, it lost force after the war.

nobi_jishin.title: Nobi Earthquake
nobi_jishin.caption: One of Japan's largest inland earthquakes, striking Gifu and Aichi. The Neodani fault shifted greatly and over 7,000 people died.

tokyo_eki.title: Tokyo Station Opens
tokyo_eki.caption: Tatsuno Kingo's red-brick station opened in Marunouchi. In 2012 it was restored to its original look, domes and all.

suiheisha.title: National Levelers Association Founded
suiheisha.caption: People who suffered discrimination formed it in Kyoto to win their own liberation. Its declaration called for warmth and light for all.

nisso.title: Soviet-Japanese Joint Declaration
nisso.caption: Signed in Moscow by Prime Minister Hatoyama Ichiro, it restored relations with the USSR. No peace treaty followed, and the island dispute remains.

isewan.title: Typhoon Vera
isewan.caption: A typhoon hit the Kii Peninsula and caused a storm surge, killing over 5,000 around Nagoya. It led to Japan's basic disaster law.

ogasawara.title: Return of the Ogasawara Islands
ogasawara.caption: The Ogasawara Islands, under US administration, were returned to Japan. They belong to Tokyo.

jnr.title: Japanese National Railways Privatized
jnr.caption: Loss-making JNR was split up and privatized as the JR companies, a key part of the Nakasone Yasuhiro cabinet's reforms.

sekai_isan.title: Japan's First World Heritage Sites
sekai_isan.caption: Horyu-ji, Himeji Castle, Yakushima and the Shirakami Mountains became Japan's first World Heritage Sites.

kyoto_giteisho.title: Kyoto Protocol Adopted
kyoto_giteisho.caption: A conference in Kyoto set targets for developed nations to cut greenhouse gases, a milestone against global warming.

world_cup_2002.title: 2002 World Cup in Japan and Korea
world_cup_2002.caption: Co-hosted by Japan and South Korea, the first soccer World Cup in Asia. Japan reached the knockout stage for the first time.

himiko_gi.title: Himiko Sends Envoys to Wei
himiko_gi.caption: The queen of Yamatai sent envoys to Wei and received the title "Ruler of Wa, Friend of Wei" and bronze mirrors, as Chinese records tell.

wao_bu.title: King Bu of Wa Writes to Song
wao_bu.caption: King Bu of Wa, thought to be Emperor Yuryaku, wrote to Song China, boasting of his conquests and asking for a high title.

kani_junikai.title: Twelve Cap Ranks
kani_junikai.caption: A system set by Prince Shotoku and others to promote officials by talent instead of family. Ranks were shown by the color of caps.

horyuji_soken.title: Horyu-ji Founded
horyuji_soken.caption: A temple said to be built by Prince Shotoku at Ikaruga. Later burned, its rebuilt western precinct is the world's oldest group of wooden buildings.

omi_sento.title: Capital Moved to Omi
omi_sento.caption: After the defeat at Baekgang, Prince Naka no Oe moved the capital to the shore of Lake Biwa. He took the throne as Emperor Tenji the next year.

kogo_nenjaku.title: Kogo Nenjaku Census
kogo_nenjaku.caption: Japan's first nationwide family register, made under Emperor Tenji. Recording the people laid the base for the ritsuryo system.

tenmu_sokui.title: Emperor Tenmu Enthroned
tenmu_sokui.caption: Prince Oama, victor of the Jinshin War, took the throne in Asuka. He ordered law codes and histories, and is said to have fixed the title "tenno."

fudoki.title: Fudoki Ordered
fudoki.caption: Empress Genmei ordered each province to report the origins of place names, local products and legends. Izumo's record survives almost whole.

yoro_ritsuryo.title: Yoro Code
yoro_ritsuryo.caption: A revision of the Taiho Code, compiled by Fujiwara no Fuhito and others. Put in force in 757, it long remained the basis of law.

kaifuso.title: Kaifuso Compiled
kaifuso.caption: Japan's oldest surviving collection of Chinese-style poems, by princes and others. It shows the learning of Nara period nobles.

ganjin.title: Ganjin Arrives in Japan
ganjin.caption: The Tang monk Ganjin reached Japan after five failed voyages and going blind. He brought formal monastic rules and set up an ordination hall at Todai-ji.

naramaro.title: Tachibana no Naramaro Plot
naramaro.caption: Naramaro plotted to overthrow the powerful Fujiwara no Nakamaro, but was betrayed, and his group was punished.

toshodaiji.title: Toshodai-ji Founded
toshodaiji.caption: A temple of the Ritsu school founded by Ganjin in Nara. Its main hall keeps its Nara period form, and a statue of Ganjin is still kept there.

kanmu_sokui.title: Emperor Kanmu Enthroned
kanmu_sokui.caption: The son of Emperor Konin took the throne. He moved the capital, fought the Emishi and reformed government, laying the base of the Heian period.

aterui.title: Aterui Surrenders
aterui.caption: Aterui, the Emishi chief who long troubled the court's armies, surrendered to Sakanoue no Tamuramaro. Despite Tamuramaro's plea, he was executed.

tendaishu.title: Saicho Founds the Tendai Sect
tendaishu.caption: Back from Tang, Saicho won official monks for the Tendai sect. Enryaku-ji on Mount Hiei became a great center of Buddhist learning.

koyasan.title: Kukai Founds Mount Koya
koyasan.caption: Emperor Saga granted Kukai Mount Koya in Kii as a place to practice esoteric Shingon Buddhism. Many believe Kukai still rests there in meditation.

jowa_no_hen.title: Jowa Incident
jowa_no_hen.caption: Tomo no Kowamine and Tachibana no Hayanari were exiled for treason. Fujiwara no Yoshifusa used it to push aside rival clans.

seiryoden.title: Lightning Strikes the Seiryoden
seiryoden.caption: Lightning hit the Seiryoden of the palace, killing nobles. People feared it was the angry spirit of Sugawara no Michizane, and his worship grew.

masakado.title: Taira no Masakado Declares Himself Emperor
masakado.caption: After attacking provincial offices in Kanto, Masakado called himself the "new emperor." He was killed the next year by Taira no Sadamori and Fujiwara no Hidesato.

anna_no_hen.title: Anna Incident
anna_no_hen.caption: Minister Minamoto no Takaakira was sent to Dazaifu on suspicion of treason. The Fujiwara had pushed out all rivals, and regents became permanent.

ojoyoshu.title: Ojoyoshu Completed
ojoyoshu.caption: A work by the monk Genshin depicting hell and paradise. It taught rebirth in paradise through the nembutsu and spread Pure Land faith.

tadatsune.title: Rebellion of Taira no Tadatsune
tadatsune.caption: A revolt by Taira no Tadatsune on the Boso Peninsula. Minamoto no Yorinobu put it down, and the Minamoto spread their power in the east.

zenkunen.title: Former Nine Years' War Begins
zenkunen.caption: A war between the Abe clan of Mutsu and the governor. Minamoto no Yoriyoshi and his son Yoshiie destroyed the Abe with help from the Kiyohara.

enkyu_shoen.title: Enkyu Estate Regulation
enkyu_shoen.caption: Emperor Go-Sanjo set up an office to check estates and abolished those without proof. Even estates of the regent family were targeted.

gosannen.title: Later Three Years' War Begins
gosannen.caption: Minamoto no Yoshiie stepped into a feud within the Kiyohara of Oshu. The survivor, Fujiwara no Kiyohira, founded the Oshu Fujiwara line.

sanjusangendo.title: Sanjusangendo Built
sanjusangendo.caption: The main hall of Rengeo-in, built by Retired Emperor Go-Shirakawa with Taira no Kiyomori's help. In the long hall stand 1,001 statues of Kannon.

samuraidokoro.title: Board of Retainers Set Up
samuraidokoro.caption: Entering Kamakura, Minamoto no Yoritomo set up an office to command his retainers. Its first head was Wada Yoshimori.

kumonjo.title: Kumonjo Office Set Up
kumonjo.caption: Yoritomo set up an office for general affairs, headed by Oe no Hiromoto from Kyoto. It later became the Mandokoro.

shugo_jito.title: Shugo and Jito Appointed
shugo_jito.caption: Yoritomo won court approval to place military governors in each province and stewards on estates. Warrior rule began to reach the whole country.

eisai.title: Eisai Brings Rinzai Zen
eisai.caption: Back from Song China, Eisai introduced Rinzai Zen. He also spread the habit of drinking tea and wrote a book on its health benefits.

tokimasa_shikken.title: Hojo Tokimasa Becomes Regent
tokimasa_shikken.caption: Tokimasa, father of Yoritomo's wife Hojo Masako, took control of the shogunate as the first regent. He later fell and retired to Izu.

rokuhara.title: Rokuhara Office Set Up
rokuhara.caption: After the Jokyu War the shogunate placed this office in Kyoto. It watched the court, led western retainers and spread shogunate power west.

hyojoshu.title: Council of State Set Up
hyojoshu.caption: Regent Hojo Yasutoki set up a council of leading retainers, so that shogunate policy was decided by discussion.

hikitsuke.title: Hikitsuke Court Set Up
hikitsuke.caption: The fifth regent, Hojo Tokiyori, set up this court to settle retainers' land suits quickly and fairly, under the Council of State.

mongol_kokusho.title: Mongol Letter Arrives
mongol_kokusho.caption: A letter from Kublai Khan reached Japan via Korea, demanding submission. The young regent Hojo Tokimune sent no reply and chose to fight.

genko_borui.title: Anti-Mongol Wall Built
genko_borui.caption: After the first invasion, the shogunate had Kyushu retainers build a stone wall along Hakata Bay. It kept the Mongols from landing the second time.

yoshimitsu_shogun.title: Ashikaga Yoshimitsu Becomes Shogun
yoshimitsu_shogun.caption: Succeeding his father Yoshiakira, he became the third shogun at just 11. He later reunited the courts and led the shogunate to its height.

meitoku_no_ran.title: Meitoku Rebellion
meitoku_no_ran.caption: Ashikaga Yoshimitsu cut down the Yamana, who held a sixth of Japan's provinces. Yamana Ujikiyo was killed in Kyoto.

yoshimitsu_daijo.title: Yoshimitsu Becomes Chancellor
yoshimitsu_daijo.caption: After handing the shogunate to his son Yoshimochi, Yoshimitsu became Grand Chancellor, the top of both warriors and court. He became a monk the next year.

zenshu_no_ran.title: Uesugi Zenshu Rebellion
zenshu_no_ran.caption: Former Kanto deputy Uesugi Ujinori (Zenshu) rebelled against Ashikaga Mochiuji, lord of Kamakura. Shogunate troops put it down.

eikyo_no_ran.title: Eikyo Rebellion
eikyo_no_ran.caption: Ashikaga Mochiuji of Kamakura rose against shogun Ashikaga Yoshinori, lost and killed himself the next year. Long turmoil in Kanto followed.

kakitsu_ikki.title: Kakitsu Uprising
kakitsu_ikki.caption: Right after the Kakitsu Incident, farmers surrounded Kyoto demanding debt relief for the new shogun's reign. The shogunate issued its first debt-cancellation decree.

yamashiro_ikki.title: Yamashiro Uprising
yamashiro_ikki.caption: Local warriors and farmers of southern Yamashiro drove out the feuding Hatakeyama armies and governed themselves for eight years.

sanpo_no_ran.title: Riot in the Three Ports
sanpo_no_ran.caption: Japanese residents of three Korean trading ports rioted against Korean controls. Trade between Japan and Korea shrank sharply.

ningbo.title: Ningbo Incident
ningbo.caption: Missions of the Ouchi and Hosokawa clans clashed at Ningbo in Ming China. Afterward the Ouchi came to monopolize the tally trade.

tenbun_hokke.title: Tenbun Hokke Disturbance
tenbun_hokke.caption: Warrior monks of Enryaku-ji burned the Nichiren temples of Kyoto, ending the self-rule of the city's Lotus sect townsmen.

kawagoe.title: Night Battle of Kawagoe
kawagoe.caption: Hojo Ujiyasu relieved Kawagoe Castle, besieged by a huge Uesugi and Ashikaga army, with a night attack. The Hojo rose to rule Kanto.

mikatagahara.title: Battle of Mikatagahara
mikatagahara.caption: Tokugawa Ieyasu challenged Takeda Shingen's westward march and was crushed. Barely escaping to Hamamatsu Castle, it was his worst defeat.

rakuichi_azuchi.title: Free Market Edict for Azuchi
rakuichi_azuchi.caption: Oda Nobunaga's edict for the town below Azuchi Castle abolished taxes and guild privileges, drawing merchants and making the town thrive.

takeda_metsubo.title: Fall of the Takeda
takeda_metsubo.caption: Oda and Tokugawa armies invaded Kai, and Takeda Katsuyori killed himself at the foot of Mount Tenmoku. The great Takeda clan was destroyed.

yamazaki.title: Battle of Yamazaki
yamazaki.caption: Soon after Honno-ji, Hashiba Hideyoshi rushed back from the west and beat Akechi Mitsuhide, whose brief rule is called the "three-day reign."

osakajo.title: Osaka Castle Begun
osakajo.caption: Hideyoshi's huge castle on the site of the Ishiyama Honganji, with gold-leaf roof tiles. Today's castle stands on Tokugawa-era foundations.

hideyoshi_kampaku.title: Hideyoshi Becomes Kanpaku
hideyoshi_kampaku.caption: Hideyoshi became the first warrior to serve as kanpaku. The next year he also became Grand Chancellor and received the name Toyotomi.

kitano_ochanoyu.title: Grand Kitano Tea Gathering
kitano_ochanoyu.caption: A huge tea party Hideyoshi held at Kitano Tenmangu in Kyoto. People of every rank were invited, and Sen no Rikyu served tea.

jurakudai.title: Jurakudai Completed
jurakudai.caption: Hideyoshi's lavish mansion in Kyoto. He received Emperor Go-Yozei there the next year and made the lords swear loyalty. It was later torn down.

kyushu_heitei.title: Hideyoshi Conquers Kyushu
kyushu_heitei.caption: Hideyoshi led a great army to Kyushu and made Shimazu Yoshihisa surrender. Western Japan came under his rule.

san_felipe.title: San Felipe Incident
san_felipe.caption: Hideyoshi seized the cargo of a Spanish ship that drifted to Tosa. It led to the martyrdom of the 26 saints the following year.

hideyoshi_shi.title: Death of Hideyoshi
hideyoshi_shi.caption: Hideyoshi died at Fushimi Castle, leaving his young son Hideyori to five regents. Troops withdrew from Korea, and Ieyasu began to rise.

tokaido_shukueki.title: Post Stations on the Tokaido
tokaido_shukueki.caption: Tokugawa Ieyasu set up post towns on the Tokaido with men and horses to carry official goods, the origin of the famous 53 stations.

hidetada_shogun.title: Tokugawa Hidetada Becomes Shogun
hidetada_shogun.caption: Ieyasu passed the post to his son Hidetada, showing the shogunate would stay with the Tokugawa. Ieyasu kept real power from Sunpu.

hirado_dutch.title: Dutch Trading Post at Hirado
hirado_dutch.caption: With Tokugawa Ieyasu's permission, the Dutch opened a trading post at Hirado. It would later be moved to Dejima.

nagoyajo.title: Nagoya Castle Begun
nagoyajo.caption: Tokugawa Ieyasu had the lords build this castle as a guard against the Toyotomi in Osaka. Its golden dolphin ornaments are famous.

kinkyo_chokkatsu.title: Christianity Banned in Shogunate Lands
kinkyo_chokkatsu.caption: The shogunate banned Christianity in its own lands, then nationwide the next year, and persecution of believers began in earnest.

hirado_english.title: English Trading Post at Hirado
hirado_english.caption: Opened at Hirado by John Saris. Losing out to the Dutch, it closed after ten years.

ikkoku_ichijo.title: One Castle per Province Law
ikkoku_ichijo.caption: Right after the Osaka sieges, lords had to tear down every castle but their own residence, cutting their military power.

kinchu_kuge.title: Laws for the Court and Nobles
kinchu_kuge.caption: Rules set by the shogunate for the emperor and court nobles, placing the imperial court under shogunate control.

genna_junkyo.title: Great Genna Martyrdom
genna_junkyo.caption: At Nishizaka in Nagasaki, 55 missionaries and believers were executed, showing how harsh the persecution of Christians was.

iemitsu_shogun.title: Tokugawa Iemitsu Becomes Shogun
iemitsu_shogun.caption: Iemitsu became the third shogun. Said to have called himself "shogun from birth," he firmly set up the shogunate's systems.

spain_kinshi.title: Spanish Ships Banned
spain_kinshi.caption: Wary of Christian missions, the shogunate banned Spanish ships, a step toward national isolation.

tokai_kinshi.title: Japanese Barred from Going Abroad
tokai_kinshi.caption: The shogunate fully banned Japanese from going abroad or returning. Japanese towns in Southeast Asia slowly faded away.

kanei_tsuho.title: Kan'ei Tsuho Coins Minted
kanei_tsuho.caption: Coins issued by the shogunate that circulated nationwide. Japan no longer had to rely on Chinese coins.

ietsuna_shogun.title: Tokugawa Ietsuna Becomes Shogun
ietsuna_shogun.caption: The young Ietsuna became the fourth shogun. Rule began to rely on law and courtesy rather than force.

nishimawari.title: Western Sea Route Opened
nishimawari.caption: The merchant Kawamura Zuiken set up a route carrying rice from Dewa around the Sea of Japan to Osaka and Edo, later used by kitamaebune ships.

echigoya.title: Mitsui Echigoya Opens
echigoya.caption: Mitsui Takatoshi opened a kimono shop in Edo that thrived by selling for cash at fixed prices. It became today's Mitsukoshi.

tsunayoshi_shogun.title: Tokugawa Tsunayoshi Becomes Shogun
tsunayoshi_shogun.caption: The fifth shogun valued Confucian learning, but his laws protecting animals earned him the name "dog shogun."

yushima_seido.title: Yushima Seido Completed
yushima_seido.caption: A Confucian temple Tsunayoshi built at Yushima in Edo. The Hayashi family school moved there, later becoming the shogunate academy.

genroku_kaichu.title: Genroku Recoinage
genroku_kaichu.caption: Finance official Ogiwara Shigehide made gold coins with less gold. The shogunate profited, but prices went up.

ako_roshi.title: Revenge of the 47 Ronin
ako_roshi.caption: Oishi Kuranosuke and 46 others stormed Kira's mansion to avenge their lord. Their story lives on as Chushingura.

kokusenya.title: The Battles of Coxinga Premieres
kokusenya.caption: Chikamatsu Monzaemon's puppet play about Coxinga's fight to restore Ming. It ran for an unheard-of 17 months.

kaihaku_goshi.title: New Rules for Nagasaki Trade
kaihaku_goshi.caption: Arai Hakuseki limited the ships and value of Nagasaki trade to stop gold and silver flowing out of Japan.

meyasubako.title: Petition Box Set Up
meyasubako.caption: Tokugawa Yoshimune placed a box for letters in front of the court in Edo. Gathering commoners' views, it led to a free clinic at Koishikawa.

agemai.title: Agemai Rice Levy
agemai.caption: Lords gave 100 koku of rice per 10,000 koku of land, and in return spent only half a year in Edo. It was one of Yoshimune's money policies.

koishikawa.title: Koishikawa Clinic Opens
koishikawa.caption: After a petition-box letter, Yoshimune opened a free clinic for poor patients. It later became a setting for novels and TV dramas.

kyoho_kikin.title: Great Kyoho Famine
kyoho_kikin.caption: Swarms of locusts and other pests caused a great famine in western Japan. The next year Edo saw its first riots against rice dealers.

kujikata.title: Kujikata Osadamegaki
kujikata.caption: Standards for trials and punishments set under Yoshimune. Its second part is known as the "Hundred Articles."

chushingura.title: Kanadehon Chushingura Premieres
chushingura.caption: A puppet play based on the Ako vendetta, set in an earlier era to avoid the shogunate's eye. It was soon staged as kabuki too.

kansei_igaku.title: Kansei Ban on Heterodox Learning
kansei_igaku.caption: Matsudaira Sadanobu banned teaching anything but Zhu Xi Confucianism at the shogunate academy, tightening control of learning.

ezochi_chokkatsu.title: Shogunate Takes Eastern Ezo
ezochi_chokkatsu.caption: To guard against Russia, the shogunate took eastern Ezo from the Matsumae domain and ruled it directly. Western Ezo followed later.

mamiya.title: Mamiya Rinzo Explores Sakhalin
mamiya.caption: On shogunate orders he explored Sakhalin and proved it an island. The strait between it and the mainland is named after him.

golovnin.title: Golovnin Incident
golovnin.caption: A Russian captain was captured on Kunashiri. In return the Russians seized the merchant Takataya Kahei, but talks settled the affair.

rangaku_kotohajime.title: Rangaku Kotohajime Completed
rangaku_kotohajime.caption: Sugita Genpaku's memoir of translating Kaitai Shinsho, written in old age. Fukuzawa Yukichi and others later published it.

uchiharai.title: Edict to Repel Foreign Ships
uchiharai.caption: The shogunate ordered that approaching foreign ships be driven off by cannon fire, after British whalers landed on its shores.

morrison_go.title: Morrison Incident
morrison_go.caption: An American ship bringing back castaways was fired upon under the repel edict. It later led to the Bansha purge.

shinsui_kyuyo.title: Tenpo Fuel and Water Order
shinsui_kyuyo.caption: Learning of Qing's defeat in the Opium War, the shogunate stopped firing on foreign ships and gave them fuel and water instead.

biddle.title: Biddle Arrives at Uraga
biddle.caption: The commander of the US East India Squadron came to Uraga seeking trade, but was refused, seven years before Perry.

putyatin.title: Putyatin Arrives at Nagasaki
putyatin.caption: A month after Perry, a Russian envoy came to Nagasaki to settle the border and seek trade.

nichiro_washin.title: Treaty of Shimoda
nichiro_washin.caption: Signed at Shimoda, it set the Japan-Russia border between Etorofu and Uruppu and made Sakhalin a shared land.

bansho_shirabesho.title: Bansho Shirabesho Set Up
bansho_shirabesho.caption: A shogunate institute in Edo for studying Western learning. It also translated diplomatic papers, and is one root of the University of Tokyo.

bunkyu_kaikaku.title: Bunkyu Reforms
bunkyu_kaikaku.caption: Pushed by Shimazu Hisamitsu, the shogunate made Tokugawa Yoshinobu guardian of the shogun and eased alternate attendance.

hachigatsu_seihen.title: Coup of August 18
hachigatsu_seihen.caption: Aizu and Satsuma joined to drive Choshu and court nobles who called for expelling foreigners out of Kyoto.

ikedaya.title: Ikedaya Incident
ikedaya.caption: The Shinsengumi stormed the Ikedaya inn in Kyoto and cut down loyalist activists. The Shinsengumi became famous overnight.

choshu_seito1.title: First Choshu Expedition
choshu_seito1.caption: After the Kinmon Incident, the shogunate sent domain armies against Choshu. Choshu punished its elders and submitted without a fight.

choshu_seito2.title: Second Choshu Expedition
choshu_seito2.caption: The shogunate attacked Choshu again, but Choshu, now allied with Satsuma, won everywhere. Shogun Iemochi's death ended the war.

osei_fukko.title: Restoration of Imperial Rule
osei_fukko.caption: Led by Iwakura Tomomi and others, it abolished the shogunate and regents and declared a new government centered on the emperor.

tokyo_kaisho.title: Edo Renamed Tokyo
tokyo_kaisho.caption: By Emperor Meiji's edict, Edo became Tokyo. The emperor moved there the next year, and Tokyo grew into Japan's capital.

kaitakushi.title: Hokkaido Development Commission
kaitakushi.caption: The Meiji government renamed Ezo as Hokkaido and set up an office to develop it. Its headquarters later moved to Sapporo.

denshin.title: Telegraph Links Tokyo and Yokohama
denshin.caption: Public telegrams began between Tokyo and Yokohama. The telegraph Perry had brought grew into a national network.

nikkan_shinbun.title: Yokohama Mainichi Shinbun Founded
nikkan_shinbun.caption: Japan's first daily newspaper in Japanese, founded in Yokohama. Printed with movable type, it opened a new age of news.

yubin.title: Postal Service Begins
yubin.caption: At Maejima Hisoka's suggestion, a state mail service began between Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka. Japanese words for "stamp" and "postcard" date from then.

shinka_jorei.title: New Currency Act
shinka_jorei.caption: The Meiji government set the units yen, sen and rin, starting a new decimal currency.

gakusei.title: Education System Ordinance
gakusei.caption: The Meiji government set up a system of elementary schools nationwide, aiming to leave no household without schooling.

gakumon_susume.title: An Encouragement of Learning
gakumon_susume.caption: Fukuzawa Yukichi's book opens "Heaven does not create one person above another" and preaches the value of learning. It was a huge bestseller.

kokuritsu_ginko.title: National Bank Act
kokuritsu_ginko.caption: A law drafted by Shibusawa Eiichi and others allowing private banks on the American model. "National" banks were not run by the state.

gasutou.title: Gas Lamps Light Yokohama
gasutou.caption: Guided by a French engineer, gas lamps were lit along Bashamichi and other streets in Yokohama, a symbol of modernization.

meiji6_seihen.title: Political Crisis of 1873
meiji6_seihen.caption: Losing the debate over invading Korea, Saigo Takamori, Itagaki Taisuke and others left the government. Okubo Toshimichi's rule began.

meirokusha.title: Meirokusha Founded
meirokusha.caption: A society for enlightenment thought begun by Mori Arinori. Fukuzawa Yukichi, Nishi Amane and others joined and put out a journal.

daiichi_ginko.title: First National Bank Opens
daiichi_ginko.caption: Japan's first bank, opened in Tokyo by Shibusawa Eiichi. It was a private bank funded by the Mitsui and Ono houses.

taiwan_shuppei.title: Taiwan Expedition
taiwan_shuppei.caption: Citing the murder of castaways from Ryukyu, the Meiji government sent troops abroad for the first time, led by Saigo Tsugumichi.

tondenhei.title: Farmer-Soldiers in Hokkaido
tondenhei.caption: To develop Hokkaido and guard the north, soldiers were settled who farmed in peacetime. Many former samurai who had lost their jobs applied.

chishima_karafuto.title: Treaty of Saint Petersburg
chishima_karafuto.caption: Signed in Russia by Enomoto Takeaki. Sakhalin became Russian, and all of the Kuril Islands became Japanese.

kokato.title: Ganghwa Island Incident
kokato.caption: A Japanese warship was fired on at Korea's Ganghwa Island and shot back. Japan used it the next year to force Korea open.

doshisha.title: Doshisha English School Founded
doshisha.caption: A Christian school opened in Kyoto by Niijima Jo after returning from America. It later became Doshisha University.

haitorei.title: Sword Abolishment Edict
haitorei.caption: Wearing swords was banned except for soldiers, police and the like. Former samurai, stripped of privileges, grew angry and revolted.

sapporo_nogakko.title: Sapporo Agricultural College Opens
sapporo_nogakko.caption: Dr. William Clark was invited as its head and left the words "Boys, be ambitious!" It became Hokkaido University.

tokyo_kabu.title: Tokyo Stock Exchange Opens
tokyo_kabu.caption: Founded through Shibusawa Eiichi's efforts, it is the forerunner of today's exchange and a foundation of Japanese capitalism.

kokkai_kisei.title: League for Establishing a National Assembly
kokkai_kisei.caption: Delegates of people's rights groups met in Osaka and petitioned the government with signatures calling for a parliament.

jiyuto.title: Liberal Party Founded
jiyuto.caption: Japan's first national party, formed by Itagaki Taisuke and others after the parliament was promised. It held radical, French-style views.

kaishinto.title: Constitutional Reform Party Founded
kaishinto.caption: Formed by Okuma Shigenobu after he was forced out of government. It aimed at moderate, British-style parliamentary politics.

tokyo_senmon.title: Tokyo Senmon Gakko Founded
tokyo_senmon.caption: A school founded by Okuma Shigenobu to keep learning independent. It later became Waseda University.

chichibu.title: Chichibu Incident
chichibu.caption: Farmers in Saitama, crushed by deflation, formed a Poor People's Party and rose up, the most famous violent episode of the rights movement.

tenshin_joyaku.title: Convention of Tientsin
tenshin_joyaku.caption: Signed by Ito Hirobumi and Li Hongzhang after a coup in Korea. Both sides withdrew troops from Korea and agreed to notify before sending more.

nippon_yusen.title: NYK Line Founded
nippon_yusen.caption: A shipping firm formed from a merger of Mitsubishi and a rival. It became the core of Japanese shipping and sailed worldwide.

hoan_jorei.title: Peace Preservation Ordinance
hoan_jorei.caption: A law letting the Meiji government banish rights activists from within 12 km of the palace. Ozaki Yukio and others were driven out of Tokyo.

shisei_chosonsei.title: Local Government System
shisei_chosonsei.caption: Led by Yamagata Aritomo, a German-style local self-government system was set up. The next year 31 cities were born.

tokaidosen.title: Tokaido Line Completed
tokaidosen.caption: Shinbashi and Kobe were joined, linking Tokyo and the Kansai by a single railway. The full trip took about 20 hours.

kitasato_hashofu.title: Kitasato Grows Pure Tetanus Bacteria
kitasato_hashofu.caption: Studying under Koch in Germany, Kitasato Shibasaburo was the first to grow tetanus bacteria alone, then moved on to serum therapy.

nichiei_tsusho.title: Anglo-Japanese Commerce Treaty
nichiei_tsusho.caption: Foreign Minister Mutsu Munemitsu got Britain to give up extraterritoriality, just before the First Sino-Japanese War.

sangoku_kansho.title: Triple Intervention
sangoku_kansho.caption: Russia, France and Germany pressed Japan to return the Liaodong Peninsula to Qing. Japanese vowed to endure and take revenge one day.

taiwan_sotokufu.title: Government-General of Taiwan
taiwan_sotokufu.caption: Set up by Japan to rule Taiwan, gained by the Treaty of Shimonoseki. Its first governor-general was Kabayama Sukenori.

meiji_sanriku.title: Meiji Sanriku Earthquake
meiji_sanriku.caption: The shaking was weak, but a huge tsunami struck the Sanriku coast and killed more than 20,000 people.

kaheiho.title: Coinage Act (Gold Standard)
kaheiho.caption: Using the war indemnity from Qing, Japan adopted the gold standard. Its currency now matched the West, steadying trade.

shiga_sekiri.title: Shiga Kiyoshi Finds the Dysentery Germ
shiga_sekiri.caption: At Kitasato's institute, Shiga found the bacterium that causes dysentery. Its scientific name, Shigella, comes from his name.

seiyukai.title: Rikken Seiyukai Founded
seiyukai.caption: A party formed by Ito Hirobumi with the old Liberal faction. It long served as one of the two great prewar parties.

chian_keisatsu.title: Public Order and Police Law
chian_keisatsu.caption: Passed by the second Yamagata cabinet to curb labor and social movements. It also banned women from political activity.

joshi_eigaku.title: Women's English School Founded
joshi_eigaku.caption: Tsuda Umeko's English school for women in Tokyo, now Tsuda University. It opened the way to higher education for women.

tanaka_jikiso.title: Tanaka Shozo's Direct Appeal
tanaka_jikiso.caption: Having quit the Diet, Tanaka Shozo ran to Emperor Meiji's carriage to plead for victims of pollution from the Ashio copper mine.

midaregami.title: Tangled Hair Published
midaregami.caption: Yosano Akiko's first collection of tanka. Its passionate poems drew wide attention.

hibiya.title: Hibiya Riots
hibiya.caption: Crowds angry that the Treaty of Portsmouth brought no indemnity attacked police boxes and newspapers in Tokyo. Martial law was declared.

mantetsu.title: South Manchuria Railway Founded
mantetsu.caption: A state-backed company running the railway won at Portsmouth. Led first by Goto Shinpei, it was the core of Japan's hold on Manchuria.

botchan.title: Natsume Soseki's Botchan
botchan.caption: Soseki's novel, published in the magazine Hototogisu. It is the lively tale of a Tokyo-born teacher posted to a school in Matsuyama.

umami.title: Ikeda Kikunae Discovers Umami
umami.caption: He extracted glutamic acid from kelp broth and named its taste "umami." It led to the business of umami seasoning.

kankoku_heigo.title: Annexation of Korea
kankoku_heigo.caption: Japan made Korea a colony by treaty. A Government-General was set up, and Japanese rule lasted until 1945.

taigyaku.title: High Treason Incident
taigyaku.caption: Kotoku Shusui and other socialists were executed for an alleged plot to kill the emperor. Many are thought to have been innocent.

oryzanin.title: Suzuki Umetaro Discovers Oryzanin
oryzanin.caption: He extracted from rice bran a substance that cured beriberi, later known as vitamin B1, a pioneering step in vitamin research.

hikoki_japan.title: First Powered Flight in Japan
hikoki_japan.caption: Tokugawa Yoshitoshi made Japan's first powered flight at Yoyogi in a French plane. Hino Kumazo also flew the same day.

seito.title: Seito Magazine Founded
seito.caption: A women's literary magazine founded by Hiratsuka Raicho and others. "In the beginning, woman was the sun," it declared, calling for women's liberation.

taisho_seihen.title: Taisho Political Crisis
taisho_seihen.caption: A movement to defend constitutional government led by Ozaki Yukio brought down the third Katsura cabinet, the first cabinet toppled by popular protest.

takarazuka.title: First Takarazuka Revue Show
takarazuka.caption: A girls' musical troupe, created by Hankyu's Kobayashi Ichizo to draw hot spring visitors, gave its first show. The Takarazuka Revue still runs today.

koshien_taikai.title: First National School Baseball Tournament
koshien_taikai.caption: The first summer tournament, ancestor of today's Koshien, held at Toyonaka in Osaka. Kyoto Second Middle School won.

siberia.title: Siberian Intervention
siberia.caption: Japan sent troops to Siberia with the US and others to intervene in the Russian Revolution. Japan stayed long and drew criticism.

shin_fujin.title: New Women's Association Founded
shin_fujin.caption: Formed by Hiratsuka Raicho, Ichikawa Fusae and others. It campaigned to change the law banning women from politics.

hara_ansatsu.title: Assassination of Hara Takashi
hara_ansatsu.caption: Prime Minister Hara was stabbed to death by a young man at Tokyo Station. The first true party cabinet ended after three years.

kyosanto.title: Japanese Communist Party Founded
kyosanto.caption: Secretly formed by Sakai Toshihiko and others. It was illegal at the time and became a legal party after the war.

koshien_kyujo.title: Koshien Stadium Completed
koshien_kyujo.caption: A big ballpark in Nishinomiya, Hyogo, finished in a "koshien" year of the calendar. It is loved as the holy ground of high school baseball.

toyoda_g.title: Toyoda Type G Automatic Loom
