toyoda_g.caption: An automatic loom by Toyoda Sakichi and others that changed shuttles without stopping. Money from its patent funded Toyota's car business.

chian_iji.title: Peace Preservation Law
chian_iji.caption: Passed the same year as universal male suffrage to suppress communism and similar ideas. It was later widely used to crush dissent.

kinyu_kyoko.title: Showa Financial Crisis
kinyu_kyoko.caption: A finance minister's slip of the tongue set off bank runs. The Tanaka Giichi cabinet calmed them with a debt moratorium.

chikatetsu.title: Japan's First Subway Opens
chikatetsu.caption: Hayakawa Noritsugu opened Asia's first subway between Ueno and Asakusa. It is now part of the Ginza Line.

sanichigo.title: March 15 Incident
sanichigo.caption: After the first universal election, the Tanaka cabinet arrested communists en masse, the first large-scale use of the Peace Preservation Law.

chosakurin.title: Assassination of Zhang Zuolin
chosakurin.caption: The Kwantung Army blew up the train of Manchurian warlord Zhang Zuolin outside Mukden. The Tanaka cabinet fell over it.

kinkaikin.title: Return to the Gold Standard
kinkaikin.caption: The Hamaguchi cabinet put Japan back on gold, but with the Great Depression it led to the Showa Depression.

london_gunshuku.title: London Naval Treaty
london_gunshuku.caption: A treaty limiting auxiliary warships, signed by the Hamaguchi cabinet. The military said it violated the emperor's command.

manshukoku.title: Manchukuo Founded
manshukoku.caption: After the Manchurian Incident, the Kwantung Army set up a state under Puyi, the last Qing emperor. Japan held the real power.

takigawa.title: Takigawa Incident
takigawa.caption: Kyoto Imperial University professor Takigawa Yukitoki was suspended for "dangerous" legal theories, a blow to academic freedom.

tenno_kikan.title: Emperor Organ Theory Incident
tenno_kikan.caption: Minobe Tatsukichi's constitutional theory was attacked in the Diet and his books banned. The government officially rejected the theory.

nichidoku_bokyo.title: Anti-Comintern Pact
nichidoku_bokyo.caption: An agreement between Japan and Germany against Soviet communism. It led to the later Tripartite Pact.

sodoinho.title: National Mobilization Law
sodoinho.caption: Preparing for a long war with China, the first Konoe cabinet let the government control people and goods.

nomonhan.title: Nomonhan Incident
nomonhan.caption: Japanese troops fought Soviet forces on the Manchuria-Mongolia border and suffered heavy losses. Plans to push north faded.

yokusankai.title: Imperial Rule Assistance Association
yokusankai.caption: Created through Konoe Fumimaro's New Order movement. All parties dissolved to join it, and it mobilized the nation for war.

nisso_churitsu.title: Soviet-Japanese Neutrality Pact
nisso_churitsu.caption: Signed in Moscow by Foreign Minister Matsuoka. In 1945 the Soviets broke it and invaded Manchuria.

yamato.title: Battleship Yamato Completed
yamato.caption: The world's largest battleship, finished at Kure with 46 cm main guns. It was sunk in 1945 on its way to Okinawa.

midway.title: Battle of Midway
midway.caption: The Japanese navy lost four of its main aircraft carriers. It was the turning point of the Pacific War.

gakuto_shutsujin.title: Students Sent to War
gakuto_shutsujin.caption: Draft deferments for humanities students and others ended, and students were sent to the front. A send-off was held at Meiji Jingu Gaien.

tokyo_daikushu.title: Great Tokyo Air Raid
tokyo_daikushu.caption: Before dawn on March 10, American B-29s firebombed Tokyo's old downtown. About 100,000 people died in one night.

hiroshima.title: Atomic Bombing of Hiroshima
hiroshima.caption: On the morning of August 6, the US used an atomic bomb in war for the first time. About 140,000 people are thought to have died that year.

tokyo_saiban.title: Tokyo War Crimes Trial Opens
tokyo_saiban.caption: The Allies tried Japan's war crimes. Tojo Hideki and six other Class-A war criminals were sentenced to death.

kyoiku_kihon.title: Fundamental Law of Education
kyoiku_kihon.caption: It set out democratic ideals for education, nine years of compulsory schooling and coeducation, replacing the Rescript on Education.

dodge_line.title: Dodge Line
dodge_line.caption: An economic plan by GHQ adviser Joseph Dodge. It fixed the rate at 360 yen to the dollar and brought inflation under control.

keisatsu_yobitai.title: National Police Reserve Created
keisatsu_yobitai.caption: Formed on MacArthur's orders after US troops in Japan left for the Korean War. It was the forerunner of the Self-Defense Forces.

jieitai.title: Self-Defense Forces Founded
jieitai.caption: The Safety Force was reorganized into ground, maritime and air forces, with a Defense Agency, to handle Japan's defense.

godzilla.title: Godzilla Released
godzilla.caption: A monster film directed by Honda Ishiro with effects by Tsuburaya Eiji. Shaped by H-bomb tests, it began a hit series worldwide.

gojugonen.title: 1955 System Begins
gojugonen.caption: The Socialists reunited and the conservatives merged into the LDP. For 38 years the LDP governed while the Socialists led the opposition.

minamata.title: Minamata Disease Confirmed
minamata.caption: A disease caused by mercury in factory waste was officially confirmed at Minamata Bay in Kumamoto. It is one of Japan's four great pollution diseases.

tokyo_tower.title: Tokyo Tower Completed
tokyo_tower.caption: A 333-meter broadcasting tower sending out TV signals. It became the symbol of Tokyo in the years of rapid growth.

instant_ramen.title: Instant Ramen Goes on Sale
instant_ramen.caption: The world's first instant ramen, developed by Ando Momofuku in a shed in Ikeda, Osaka. Just add hot water.

shotoku_baizo.title: Income-Doubling Plan
shotoku_baizo.caption: The Ikeda Hayato cabinet's plan to double national income in ten years. It was actually achieved in about seven.

tetsuwan_atom.title: Astro Boy Begins Airing
tetsuwan_atom.caption: Based on Tezuka Osamu's manga, it aired as Japan's first full-fledged animated TV series.

nikkan_kihon.title: Japan-Korea Basic Treaty
nikkan_kihon.caption: Signed by the Sato Eisaku cabinet with South Korea. It opened relations and promised economic cooperation.

tomonaga.title: Tomonaga Shin'ichiro Wins the Nobel Prize
tomonaga.caption: For his work on quantum electrodynamics, he became the second Japanese, after Yukawa, to win the Nobel Prize in Physics.

kogai_kihon.title: Basic Law for Pollution Control
kogai_kihon.caption: Passed after the four great pollution disasters. It set the duties of companies and the state and laid the base for anti-pollution policy.

osumi.title: Satellite Ohsumi Launched
osumi.caption: Japan's first satellite, launched by the University of Tokyo from Uchinoura. Japan became the fourth nation in orbit after the USSR, US and France.

kankyocho.title: Environment Agency Founded
kankyocho.caption: Set up by the government as pollution problems grew. It is now the Ministry of the Environment.

sapporo_olympic.title: Sapporo Winter Olympics
sapporo_olympic.caption: The first Winter Olympics in Asia. Japanese jumpers swept the podium on the normal hill.

asama_sanso.title: Asama-Sanso Incident
asama_sanso.caption: Members of the United Red Army held a hostage in a mountain lodge in Nagano. The wrecking-ball raid was shown live on TV.

sanyo_shinkansen.title: Sanyo Shinkansen Completed
sanyo_shinkansen.caption: The line reached Hakata, joining Tokyo and Fukuoka by bullet train. It crosses the Kanmon Strait by tunnel.

kaiyohaku.title: Okinawa Ocean Expo
kaiyohaku.caption: An expo in Motobu, Okinawa, marking Okinawa's return to Japan, on the theme "The Sea We Would Like to See."

lockheed.title: Lockheed Scandal Exposed
lockheed.caption: A bribery scandal over aircraft sales came out in US Senate hearings. Former Prime Minister Tanaka Kakuei was arrested.

nicchu_heiwa.title: Japan-China Peace and Friendship Treaty
nicchu_heiwa.caption: Signed in Beijing by the Fukuda Takeo cabinet, carrying on the spirit of the 1972 joint statement.

walkman.title: Walkman Goes on Sale
walkman.caption: Sony's small cassette player. It spread the culture of taking music outdoors around the world.

tohoku_shinkansen.title: Tohoku Shinkansen Opens
tohoku_shinkansen.caption: The line opened between Omiya and Morioka. The Joetsu Shinkansen opened that autumn.

famicom.title: Family Computer Goes on Sale
famicom.caption: Nintendo's home game console. It spread the culture of playing games on the family TV.

tdl.title: Tokyo Disneyland Opens
tdl.caption: Opened in Urayasu, Chiba, the first Disney park outside the United States.

plaza_accord.title: Plaza Accord
plaza_accord.caption: At New York's Plaza Hotel, five major nations agreed to bring down the dollar. The yen rose, one cause of the bubble economy.

jal123.title: JAL Flight 123 Crash
jal123.caption: A jumbo jet crashed on Osutaka Ridge in Gunma, killing 520 people, the worst single-plane accident in history.

seto_ohashi.title: Great Seto Bridge Opens
seto_ohashi.caption: The first bridges linking Honshu and Shikoku, joining Okayama and Kagawa, with a railway below and a road above.

heisei.title: Heisei Era Begins
heisei.caption: After Emperor Showa's death the era name changed. Chief Cabinet Secretary Obuchi Keizo held up the characters for "Heisei."

shohizei.title: Consumption Tax Introduced
shohizei.caption: The Takeshita Noboru cabinet brought in a 3% sales tax, paid on every purchase.

unzen.title: Pyroclastic Flow at Mount Unzen
unzen.caption: A pyroclastic flow on Mount Fugen in Nagasaki killed 43 people, including reporters and volcanologists.

pko_ho.title: UN Peacekeeping Law
pko_ho.caption: A law allowing Japan to join UN peacekeeping. The Self-Defense Forces were sent to Cambodia.

kix.title: Kansai International Airport Opens
kix.caption: Built on a man-made island in Osaka Bay, it was Japan's first international airport to run 24 hours a day.

oe_kenzaburo.title: Oe Kenzaburo Wins the Nobel Prize
oe_kenzaburo.caption: The author of The Silent Cry became the second Japanese to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.

sarin.title: Tokyo Subway Sarin Attack
sarin.caption: Members of Aum Shinrikyo released deadly sarin gas on Tokyo subway trains. Fourteen people died and over 6,000 were hurt.

shirakawago.title: Shirakawa-go and Gokayama World Heritage
shirakawago.caption: Villages of steep thatched-roof houses in Gifu and Toyama became World Heritage Sites.

genbaku_dome.title: Atomic Bomb Dome World Heritage
genbaku_dome.caption: The building that shows the horror of the bombing became a World Heritage Site, a leading example of "dark heritage."

itsukushima_whs.title: Itsukushima Shrine World Heritage
itsukushima_whs.caption: The shrine famed for its great gate and halls that seem to float on the sea became a World Heritage Site. It flourished with Taira no Kiyomori's support.

yamaichi.title: Collapse of Yamaichi Securities
yamaichi.caption: One of the big four brokerages failed over huge hidden debts. Its president's tearful press conference became a symbol of the Heisei slump.

akashi_ohashi.title: Akashi Kaikyo Bridge Opens
akashi_ohashi.caption: The world's longest suspension bridge at the time, 3,911 meters, linking Kobe and Awaji Island.

chuetsu.title: Chuetsu Earthquake
chuetsu.caption: A quake struck central Niigata. A Joetsu Shinkansen train derailed in service for the first time, and the whole village of Yamakoshi was evacuated.

yusei_mineika.title: Postal Privatization
yusei_mineika.caption: A reform pushed by the Koizumi Junichiro cabinet took effect, and the Japan Post Group was born.

seiken_kotai.title: Democratic Party Takes Power
seiken_kotai.caption: The DPJ won a landslide and the Hatoyama Yukio cabinet took office. For the first time the LDP lost its place as the largest party.

hayabusa.title: Hayabusa Returns to Earth
hayabusa.caption: The probe brought back dust from the asteroid Itokawa, returning after seven years despite many breakdowns.

kyushu_shinkansen.title: Kyushu Shinkansen Completed
kyushu_shinkansen.caption: Hakata and Kagoshima-Chuo were joined by bullet train. It opened the day after the Great East Japan Earthquake, and the celebrations were canceled.

yamanaka.title: Yamanaka Shinya Wins the Nobel Prize
yamanaka.caption: The Kyoto University professor who created iPS cells, able to grow into any type of cell, won the Nobel Prize in Medicine.

fuji_whs.title: Mount Fuji World Heritage
fuji_whs.caption: Listed as a World Heritage Site as "place of worship and source of artistic inspiration." The Miho pine grove is part of the site.

ontake.title: Eruption of Mount Ontake
ontake.caption: It erupted suddenly on an autumn weekend, leaving 63 climbers dead or missing, Japan's worst volcanic disaster since the war.

hokkaido_shinkansen.title: Hokkaido Shinkansen Opens
hokkaido_shinkansen.caption: The line opened between Shin-Aomori and Shin-Hakodate-Hokuto, linking Honshu and Hokkaido by bullet train through the Seikan Tunnel.

kumamoto_jishin.title: Kumamoto Earthquakes
kumamoto_jishin.caption: Quakes reached the top intensity of 7 twice in a row. Kumamoto Castle's stone walls and keep were badly damaged.

reiwa.title: Reiwa Era Begins
reiwa.caption: The era name changed with the emperor's abdication. Taken from the Man'yoshu, it is the first era name drawn from a Japanese classic.

kinkyu_jitai.title: COVID-19 State of Emergency
kinkyu_jitai.caption: Prime Minister Abe Shinzo declared an emergency for seven prefectures, later nationwide. Schools and shops closed.

tokyo2020.title: Tokyo 2020 Games Held
tokyo2020.caption: Postponed a year by the pandemic, they were held mostly without spectators. Japan won 27 gold medals.

noto_jishin.title: New Year's Day Noto Earthquake
noto_jishin.caption: A great quake struck the Noto Peninsula in Ishikawa on the evening of January 1. It reached intensity 7, and Wajima's morning market street burned.

osaka_expo2025.title: Expo 2025 Osaka Opens
osaka_expo2025.caption: A world's fair on Yumeshima in Osaka on the theme "Designing Future Society for Our Lives." Its giant wooden Grand Ring became an icon.

first_olympiad.title: First Ancient Olympics
first_olympiad.caption: At Olympia in Greece, games honoring Zeus began to be recorded. Held every four years, they lasted over a thousand years.

marathon.title: Battle of Marathon
marathon.caption: Athenian hoplites defeated the Persian army. The tale of a runner who carried news of the victory gave the marathon its name.

thermopylae.title: Battle of Thermopylae
thermopylae.caption: A small force under King Leonidas of Sparta held off the huge Persian army in a narrow pass and fought to the last man.

salamis.title: Battle of Salamis
salamis.caption: A Greek fleet under Themistocles beat the Persian fleet in a narrow strait, turning the tide of the Persian Wars.

death_of_socrates.title: Death of Socrates
death_of_socrates.caption: The philosopher Socrates was tried in Athens for corrupting the young and died by drinking poison.

alexander_east.title: Alexander's Eastern Campaign
alexander_east.caption: The young king of Macedon set out east. He destroyed the Persian Empire and marched almost to the Indus River.

qin_unification.title: Qin Unifies China
qin_unification.caption: King Zheng of Qin destroyed the six rival states, united China for the first time and called himself the First Emperor. He standardized writing, coins and measures.

cannae.title: Battle of Cannae
cannae.caption: Hannibal of Carthage surrounded and wiped out a huge Roman army. It is still studied as the model of encirclement.

fall_of_carthage.title: Fall of Carthage
fall_of_carthage.caption: In the third war, Rome razed the city of Carthage. Rome now ruled the Mediterranean.

caesar_assassination.title: Assassination of Caesar
caesar_assassination.caption: Caesar, dictator for life, was stabbed to death in the Senate by Brutus and others: "You too, Brutus?"

actium.title: Battle of Actium
actium.caption: Octavian defeated the forces of Antony and Cleopatra, ending Rome's civil wars.

vesuvius.title: Eruption of Vesuvius Buries Pompeii
vesuvius.caption: An eruption of Mount Vesuvius buried Pompeii in ash. The excavated town shows daily life in ancient Rome.

red_cliffs.title: Battle of Red Cliffs
red_cliffs.caption: Sun Quan and Liu Bei used fire to rout Cao Cao's huge army. China moved toward three kingdoms, a highlight of the Three Kingdoms story.

edict_of_milan.title: Edict of Milan
edict_of_milan.caption: Emperors Constantine and Licinius legalized Christianity, ending a long period of persecution.

nicaea.title: First Council of Nicaea
nicaea.caption: The first church council, called by Constantine. It upheld Athanasius's teaching and declared Arianism a heresy.

rome_division.title: Roman Empire Divided
rome_division.caption: At Theodosius's death the empire was split between his two sons. The division between East and West became permanent.

fall_of_western_rome.title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
fall_of_western_rome.caption: The Germanic mercenary leader Odoacer deposed the boy emperor, and the Western Roman Empire came to an end.

hijra.title: The Hijra
hijra.caption: Muhammad fled persecution, moving from Mecca to Medina. This year is the first year of the Islamic calendar.

tours.title: Battle of Tours
tours.caption: Charles Martel of the Franks stopped the northward advance of a Muslim army.

charlemagne.title: Coronation of Charlemagne
charlemagne.caption: Charles, king of the Franks, was crowned emperor by the Pope in Rome, a symbol of a united Western Europe.

treaty_of_verdun.title: Treaty of Verdun
treaty_of_verdun.caption: The Frankish realm was split into three among Charlemagne's grandsons, the roots of Germany, France and Italy.

otto_coronation.title: Coronation of Otto I
otto_coronation.caption: King Otto of Germany was crowned emperor by the Pope, seen as the start of the Holy Roman Empire.

hastings.title: Battle of Hastings
hastings.caption: William, Duke of Normandy, defeated King Harold of England. The Norman dynasty began, even changing the English language.

first_crusade.title: First Crusade
first_crusade.caption: Called by Pope Urban II, armies of Western lords took Jerusalem and founded crusader states.

genghis_khan.title: Genghis Khan Proclaimed
genghis_khan.caption: Temujin united the Mongol tribes and was hailed as Great Khan. The largest empire in history began to grow.

magna_carta.title: Magna Carta
magna_carta.caption: A charter English barons forced King John to accept. The idea that even the king is under the law became a basis of constitutional rule.

hundred_years_war.title: Hundred Years' War Begins
hundred_years_war.caption: A long war between England and France began over the French throne and Flanders. It lasted until 1453.

ming_founding.title: Ming Dynasty Founded
ming_founding.caption: Zhu Yuanzhang, risen from the Red Turban revolt, took the throne in Nanjing and drove the Mongol Yuan north.

fall_of_constantinople.title: Fall of Constantinople
fall_of_constantinople.caption: Mehmed II of the Ottomans broke the walls with cannon, ending the Eastern Roman Empire.

granada.title: Fall of Granada
granada.caption: The Catholic Monarchs took the last Muslim kingdom in Iberia, completing the Reconquista.

columbus.title: Columbus Reaches America
columbus.caption: Backed by Spain, he crossed the Atlantic. Still believing he had reached the Indies, he linked Europe and the Americas.

vasco_da_gama.title: Vasco da Gama Reaches India
vasco_da_gama.caption: The Portuguese navigator rounded the Cape of Good Hope and reached Calicut, opening a sea route between Europe and Asia.

ninety_five_theses.title: Luther's Ninety-Five Theses
ninety_five_theses.caption: Luther's attack on the sale of indulgences. From Wittenberg, the Reformation spread across Europe.

magellan.title: Magellan Sets Out
magellan.caption: He led a Spanish fleet west. He was killed in the Philippines, but his crew completed the first voyage around the world.

aztec_fall.title: Fall of the Aztec Empire
aztec_fall.caption: The Spaniard Cortes captured the capital Tenochtitlan. Guns, horses and smallpox brought down the empire.

armada.title: Defeat of the Spanish Armada
armada.caption: The English fleet beat Spain's "Invincible Armada." Under Elizabeth I, England's reach across the seas grew.

east_india_company.title: East India Company Founded
east_india_company.caption: A trading company chartered by Elizabeth I. In time it came to rule India itself.

thirty_years_war.title: Thirty Years' War Begins
thirty_years_war.caption: A religious war sparked by a Protestant revolt in Bohemia. It drew in Europe's great powers and laid Germany waste.

mayflower.title: Voyage of the Mayflower
mayflower.caption: The ship carried the Pilgrim Fathers from England to America. Their story gave rise to Thanksgiving.

westphalia.title: Peace of Westphalia
westphalia.caption: The treaties ending the Thirty Years' War, seen as the start of a Europe of sovereign states.

principia.title: Newton's Principia
principia.caption: Newton's book explaining universal gravitation and the laws of motion in mathematics, a landmark of modern science.

glorious_revolution.title: Glorious Revolution
glorious_revolution.caption: Parliament drove out James II and invited William III from the Netherlands. The Bill of Rights set Parliament above the crown.

us_independence.title: US Declaration of Independence
us_independence.caption: Drafted by Jefferson and others and adopted on July 4, it declared 13 colonies independent from Britain.

bastille.title: Storming of the Bastille
bastille.caption: On July 14 the people of Paris stormed the prison. It began the French Revolution, and the day is still France's national day.

napoleon_emperor.title: Napoleon Crowned Emperor
napoleon_emperor.caption: After a national vote, Napoleon became emperor. He is said to have crowned himself at Notre-Dame.

trafalgar.title: Battle of Trafalgar
trafalgar.caption: Admiral Nelson's British fleet defeated the combined French and Spanish fleets. Nelson was killed in the battle.

russian_campaign.title: Napoleon's Russian Campaign
russian_campaign.caption: Napoleon invaded Russia with some 600,000 men but was beaten by scorched earth and bitter cold. His empire began to fall.

waterloo.title: Battle of Waterloo
waterloo.caption: The returned Napoleon was beaten by Wellington and the Prussians, then exiled to Saint Helena.

opium_war.title: Opium War Begins
opium_war.caption: Britain went to war when Qing cracked down on opium. Qing lost and gave up Hong Kong.

origin_of_species.title: On the Origin of Species
origin_of_species.caption: Darwin set out his theory of evolution by natural selection, changing not just biology but how we see the world.

us_civil_war.title: American Civil War Begins
us_civil_war.caption: Over slavery, the South left the Union and fought the North. Lincoln's North won, and slavery was abolished.

gettysburg_address.title: Gettysburg Address
gettysburg_address.caption: Lincoln's short speech honoring the war dead, known for "government of the people, by the people, for the people."

suez_canal.title: Suez Canal Opens
suez_canal.caption: Led by the Frenchman Lesseps, it linked the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, greatly shortening the trip between Asia and Europe.

german_empire.title: German Empire Proclaimed
german_empire.caption: Amid victory over France, Wilhelm I became emperor at Versailles, completing Bismarck's unification.

telephone.title: Bell Patents the Telephone
telephone.caption: Bell received the patent for the telephone. A rival claim by Gray, filed the same day, led to long lawsuits.

eiffel_tower.title: Eiffel Tower Completed
eiffel_tower.caption: An iron tower built for the Paris Exposition. First attacked as an eyesore, it became the symbol of Paris.

wright_brothers.title: Wright Brothers' First Flight
wright_brothers.caption: The brothers flew the first powered airplane on the North Carolina coast. The first flight lasted just 12 seconds.

titanic.title: Sinking of the Titanic
titanic.caption: On its maiden voyage the luxury liner hit an iceberg and sank. Without enough lifeboats, over 1,500 people died.

ww1_outbreak.title: World War I Begins
ww1_outbreak.caption: After the Sarajevo assassination, Europe's great powers joined in one after another through alliances. Tanks and poison gas appeared.

russian_revolution.title: Russian Revolution Topples the Romanovs
russian_revolution.caption: People suffering from war and hunger rose up and Nicholas II abdicated. Later that year Lenin and his party took power.

penicillin.title: Discovery of Penicillin
penicillin.caption: Fleming found by chance that a blue mold killed bacteria, opening the age of antibiotics.

great_depression.title: Great Depression Begins
great_depression.caption: It began with a crash on the New York stock market. Joblessness spread worldwide and helped lead to war.

ww2_outbreak.title: World War II Begins
ww2_outbreak.caption: Germany invaded Poland, and Britain and France declared war. The fighting spread across the globe in the largest war in history.

united_nations.title: United Nations Founded
united_nations.caption: Born with 51 members after the San Francisco Conference. Learning from the League, it gave the Security Council strong powers.

prc_founding.title: People's Republic of China Founded
prc_founding.caption: After winning the civil war, Mao Zedong proclaimed the new state at Tiananmen in Beijing. The defeated Nationalists fled to Taiwan.

sputnik.title: Sputnik 1 Launched
sputnik.caption: The Soviet Union launched the world's first satellite. It shocked America and began the space race.

cuban_missile.title: Cuban Missile Crisis
cuban_missile.caption: Soviet missiles in Cuba brought the US and USSR to the brink of nuclear war. After 13 tense days, the Soviets agreed to remove them.

apollo11.title: Apollo 11 Moon Landing
apollo11.caption: Armstrong became the first person to walk on the Moon: "one giant leap for mankind."

berlin_wall_fall.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
berlin_wall_fall.caption: When East Germany announced free travel, crowds rushed the Wall. It became the symbol of the Cold War's end.

ussr_dissolution.title: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
ussr_dissolution.caption: President Gorbachev resigned and the USSR broke into independent states. A socialist giant of nearly 70 years was gone.

joan_orleans.title: Joan of Arc Relieves Orleans
joan_orleans.caption: Joan, a peasant girl who said she heard God's voice, broke the English siege. She was later burned as a heretic.

copernicus.title: Copernicus's On the Revolutions
copernicus.caption: Copernicus's book arguing that the Earth goes around the Sun, published just before his death.

galileo_moons.title: Galileo Finds Jupiter's Moons
galileo_moons.caption: With his homemade telescope Galileo found four moons of Jupiter, showing that not everything in the sky circles the Earth.

versailles.title: Treaty of Versailles
versailles.caption: The peace treaty ending World War I. Germany was charged huge reparations, and the anger helped the Nazis rise.

german_reunification.title: German Reunification
german_reunification.caption: West Germany absorbed East Germany, less than a year after the fall of the Berlin Wall.

alexander_death.title: Death of Alexander the Great
alexander_death.caption: Alexander died in Babylon at just 32. His vast empire was split up by his feuding generals.

zama.title: Battle of Zama
zama.caption: Scipio Africanus defeated Hannibal in North Africa, ending the Second Punic War in Rome's favor.

augustus.title: Octavian Named Augustus
augustus.caption: The Senate gave Octavian the title Augustus, "the revered one." Rule by Roman emperors began.

cai_lun_paper.title: Cai Lun Presents Paper
cai_lun_paper.caption: Cai Lun, a eunuch of the Later Han, presented the emperor with paper made from bark and rags. He is known as the improver of papermaking.

great_schism.title: East-West Schism
great_schism.caption: The Pope and the Patriarch of Constantinople excommunicated each other, splitting the Catholic and Orthodox churches.

marco_polo.title: Marco Polo Sets Out
marco_polo.caption: The son of a Venetian merchant traveled east with his father. He served Kublai Khan and left The Travels of Marco Polo.

augsburg.title: Peace of Augsburg
augsburg.caption: Princes of the Holy Roman Empire could choose Lutheranism or Catholicism, though individuals still had no freedom of belief.

lepanto.title: Battle of Lepanto
lepanto.caption: The fleet of Spain and its Holy League allies defeated the Ottoman fleet. Cervantes, author of Don Quixote, was wounded there.

vienna_1683.title: Second Siege of Vienna
vienna_1683.caption: An Ottoman army besieged Vienna but was routed by Polish relief forces. The empire's long retreat began.

watt_engine.title: Watt Patents His Steam Engine
watt_engine.caption: Watt patented his improved steam engine. Powering factories, it drove the Industrial Revolution forward.

communist_manifesto.title: The Communist Manifesto
communist_manifesto.caption: Written by Marx and Engels, it closes with the call "Workers of the world, unite!"

lincoln_assassination.title: Assassination of Lincoln
lincoln_assassination.caption: Just after the Civil War ended, Lincoln was shot by the actor Booth in a Washington theater.

athens_1896.title: First Modern Olympics
athens_1896.caption: Proposed by Coubertin, they were held in Greece, home of the ancient games. Only men took part, from 14 nations.

xinhai.title: Xinhai Revolution
xinhai.caption: A revolt at Wuchang spread across China. Qing fell the next year, ending more than 2,000 years of imperial rule.

dna_helix.title: Double Helix of DNA
dna_helix.caption: Watson and Crick announced the double-helix structure of DNA, opening the age of molecular biology.

solon.title: Reforms of Solon
solon.caption: The Athenian archon cancelled debts and sorted citizens into classes, a step toward later democracy.

peloponnesian.title: Peloponnesian War Begins
peloponnesian.caption: Athens and its Delian League began fighting Sparta and its allies, drawing in the whole Greek world.

punic_first.title: First Punic War Begins
punic_first.caption: Rome and Carthage began fighting over Sicily. Rome built a navy and won after 23 years.

spartacus.title: Revolt of Spartacus
spartacus.caption: The gladiator Spartacus escaped his school and led tens of thousands of slaves in revolt. He was crushed by Crassus.

rubicon.title: Caesar Crosses the Rubicon
rubicon.caption: Back from Gaul, Caesar led his army across the river and marched on Rome, saying, it is told, "The die is cast."

teutoburg.title: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest
teutoburg.caption: Arminius and his Germanic warriors wiped out three Roman legions. Rome gave up conquering lands beyond the Rhine.

rome_fire.title: Great Fire of Rome
rome_fire.caption: A fire burned most of Rome. Tacitus says Emperor Nero blamed and persecuted the Christians.

colosseum.title: Colosseum Completed
colosseum.caption: The great amphitheater was finished under Emperor Titus. Fifty thousand spectators cheered gladiator fights there.

yellow_turban.title: Yellow Turban Rebellion
yellow_turban.caption: A peasant revolt led by Zhang Jue of the Way of Great Peace. It shook the Later Han and began the age of the Three Kingdoms.

constantinople_founded.title: Constantinople Becomes the Capital
constantinople_founded.caption: Constantine moved the Roman capital to Byzantium. For over a thousand years it remained the imperial city of the East.

catalaunian.title: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains
catalaunian.caption: The Roman general Aetius and his Germanic allies turned back Attila's Huns in Gaul.

hagia_sophia.title: Hagia Sophia Completed
hagia_sophia.caption: The cathedral rebuilt by Emperor Justinian, a masterpiece of Byzantine building with a huge dome. It later became a mosque.

sui_unification.title: Sui Unifies China
sui_unification.caption: Emperor Wen of Sui conquered the Chen and reunited China after about 300 years. The Sui also began the civil service exams.

tang_founding.title: Tang Dynasty Founded
tang_founding.caption: Amid the chaos at the end of Sui, Li Yuan took the throne in Chang'an. With its laws and cosmopolitan culture, Tang led East Asia.

baghdad.title: Founding of Baghdad
baghdad.caption: The Abbasid caliph al-Mansur built a round city on the Tigris. It became the setting of the Thousand and One Nights.

song_founding.title: Song Dynasty Founded
song_founding.caption: The general Zhao Kuangyin made himself emperor and founded Song. Favoring civil officials, it saw great growth in economy and culture.

canossa.title: Walk to Canossa
canossa.caption: To have his excommunication lifted, Emperor Henry IV begged Pope Gregory VII for forgiveness in the snow for three days.

saladin.title: Saladin Retakes Jerusalem
saladin.caption: Saladin, founder of the Ayyubid dynasty, took Jerusalem back from the crusaders. Even his enemies praised his mercy.

baghdad_fall.title: Mongols Take Baghdad
baghdad_fall.caption: Hulagu's Mongol army destroyed the city and ended the Abbasid caliphate, a great shock to the Islamic world.

zheng_he.title: Zheng He's First Voyage
zheng_he.caption: On the Yongle Emperor's orders, he led a great fleet into the southern seas. Later voyages reached the east coast of Africa.

agincourt.title: Battle of Agincourt
agincourt.caption: Henry V of England defeated a larger French army with the longbow. It is famous from Shakespeare's play.

dias.title: Dias Rounds the Cape
dias.caption: The Portuguese navigator sailed around Africa's southern tip. Named the Cape of Good Hope, it opened the way to India.

tordesillas.title: Treaty of Tordesillas
tordesillas.caption: With papal backing, Spain and Portugal drew a line dividing the world. This is why Brazil speaks Portuguese.

balboa.title: Balboa Reaches the Pacific
balboa.caption: The Spaniard Balboa crossed the Isthmus of Panama and became the first European to see the Pacific.

mughal.title: Mughal Empire Founded
mughal.caption: Babur defeated the Lodi dynasty at Panipat and founded an empire in India.

vienna_1529.title: First Siege of Vienna
vienna_1529.caption: Suleiman I of the Ottomans besieged Vienna but withdrew as winter came. It shocked Europe.

inca_fall.title: Execution of Atahualpa
inca_fall.caption: The Spaniard Pizarro captured and executed the Inca emperor, and the Inca Empire headed for its end.

trent.title: Council of Trent Opens
trent.caption: In answer to the Reformation, the Catholic Church restated its teachings at a council held on and off for about 18 years.

nantes.title: Edict of Nantes
nantes.caption: King Henry IV of France granted the Huguenots freedom of worship, ending the French Wars of Religion.

charles_execution.title: Execution of Charles I
charles_execution.caption: In the English Civil War, Cromwell and others executed the king, and England became a republic without a monarch.

louis_xiv.title: Louis XIV Takes Personal Rule
louis_xiv.caption: After Cardinal Mazarin died, Louis XIV began to rule by himself. Under the "Sun King," French absolute monarchy reached its height.

nerchinsk.title: Treaty of Nerchinsk
nerchinsk.caption: Qing China and Russia signed it, Qing's first treaty between equals, fixing the border along the Amur River.

st_petersburg.title: St. Petersburg Founded
st_petersburg.caption: Peter the Great began building a capital on marshland at the edge of the Baltic, called Russia's "window on the West."

plassey.title: Battle of Plassey
plassey.caption: Robert Clive of the East India Company beat the Nawab of Bengal and his French allies, a foothold for British rule in India.

boston_tea.title: Boston Tea Party
boston_tea.caption: Angry at the Tea Act, colonists dumped chests of tea from ships into the harbor, a prelude to the War of Independence.

montgolfier.title: Montgolfier Balloon Flight
montgolfier.caption: In a hot-air balloon made by the brothers, people flew for the first time, drifting over Paris for about 25 minutes.

louis_xvi.title: Execution of Louis XVI
louis_xvi.caption: Put on trial during the Revolution, the king was guillotined. Queen Marie Antoinette was executed later that year.

jenner.title: Jenner's Smallpox Vaccine
jenner.caption: An English doctor used cowpox to protect against smallpox, the birth of vaccination.

congress_vienna.title: Congress of Vienna Opens
congress_vienna.caption: Powers met to rebuild order after the Napoleonic Wars. Led by Metternich, it was mocked as "the Congress dances."

stockton.title: Stockton and Darlington Railway Opens
stockton.caption: The world's first public railway, running Stephenson's steam locomotive. The railway age began.

july_revolution.title: July Revolution
july_revolution.caption: Parisians overthrew Charles X. Delacroix's painting Liberty Leading the People depicts this revolution.

great_exhibition.title: Great Exhibition in London
great_exhibition.caption: The first world's fair, held in the Crystal Palace in Queen Victoria's time. It showed off Britain's industrial might.

alaska.title: Purchase of Alaska
alaska.caption: The US bought Alaska from Russia for 7.2 million dollars. Mocked as "Seward's Folly," it later yielded gold and oil.

transcontinental.title: First Transcontinental Railroad
transcontinental.caption: Lines from east and west met in Utah, where a golden spike was driven. America was joined by rail.

edison_bulb.title: Edison's Light Bulb
edison_bulb.caption: Edison made a practical, long-lasting light bulb. Bamboo from Kyoto was later used for its filament.

xray.title: Roentgen Discovers X-rays
xray.caption: The German Roentgen found unknown rays that passed through matter. He won the first Nobel Prize in Physics.

relativity.title: Einstein's Special Relativity
relativity.caption: Einstein, a patent clerk, overturned common sense about time and space in one of his "miracle year" papers.

lindbergh.title: Lindbergh Flies the Atlantic Solo
lindbergh.caption: In the Spirit of St. Louis he flew nonstop from New York to Paris in about 33 and a half hours.

bandung.title: Bandung Conference
bandung.caption: Twenty-nine nations met in Bandung, Indonesia. Countries newly freed from colonial rule adopted ten principles of peace.

gagarin.title: Gagarin Flies into Space
gagarin.caption: The Soviet cosmonaut circled the Earth in Vostok 1, becoming the first human in space.

cyrus_babylon.title: Cyrus II Enters Babylon
cyrus_babylon.caption: The Persian king took Babylon without a fight. He is also known for freeing the Jews held captive there.

parthenon.title: Parthenon Begun
parthenon.caption: In Pericles's time, work began on this temple to Athena on the Acropolis, a masterpiece of Greek architecture.

chaeronea.title: Battle of Chaeronea
chaeronea.caption: Philip II of Macedon defeated Athens and Thebes. Young Prince Alexander also fought bravely.

gaugamela.title: Battle of Gaugamela
gaugamela.caption: Alexander the Great defeated the Persian king Darius III, sealing the fall of the Achaemenid Empire.

liu_bang.title: Liu Bang Becomes Emperor (Han Founded)
liu_bang.caption: Having beaten Xiang Yu, Liu Bang became emperor and founded Han. He rose from peasant to emperor.

gracchi.title: Reforms of the Gracchi
gracchi.caption: Two brothers, tribunes of the people, tried to limit large estates and help farmers. Both were killed, and Rome entered a century of civil strife.

later_han.title: Later Han Founded
later_han.caption: Emperor Guangwu, Liu Xiu, restored Han after Wang Mang's Xin and moved the capital from Chang'an to Luoyang.

han_fall.title: Fall of the Han
han_fall.caption: Cao Pi made Emperor Xian give up the throne and founded Wei. The Han, some 400 years old, fell, and the Three Kingdoms began.

sack_of_rome.title: Visigoths Sack Rome
sack_of_rome.caption: Alaric's Visigoths entered and looted the Eternal City, shocking the Roman world.

justinian_code.title: Code of Justinian
justinian_code.caption: Emperor Justinian had Tribonian and others compile Roman law, the foundation of European law.

umayyad.title: Umayyad Caliphate Founded
umayyad.caption: Muawiya founded a dynasty ruling from Damascus. The caliphate became hereditary, deepening the split of Sunni and Shia.

an_lushan.title: An Lushan Rebellion
an_lushan.caption: The general An Lushan rebelled after feuding with Yang Guifei's family. Tang's golden age ended, and Emperor Xuanzong fled.

vladimir_baptism.title: Baptism of Vladimir of Kiev
vladimir_baptism.caption: The Grand Prince of Kiev accepted Christianity as the state religion. Orthodoxy became a base of Russian culture.

notre_dame.title: Notre-Dame de Paris Begun
notre_dame.caption: Work began on this Gothic cathedral on the Ile de la Cite. It took about 200 years and was rebuilt after a fire in 2019.

legnica.title: Battle of Legnica
legnica.caption: Batu's Mongol army defeated Polish and German forces, spreading terror across Europe.

ottoman.title: Ottoman Empire Founded
ottoman.caption: A state said to be founded by Osman I in northwest Anatolia. It grew into an empire spanning three continents.

ankara.title: Battle of Ankara
ankara.caption: Timur defeated and captured the Ottoman sultan Bayezid I. For a time the Ottoman state nearly collapsed.

grunwald.title: Battle of Grunwald
grunwald.caption: Polish and Lithuanian forces crushed the Teutonic Knights in one of the largest battles of medieval Europe.

jesuits.title: Society of Jesus Founded
jesuits.caption: Ignatius of Loyola, Francis Xavier and others took vows in Paris. The order went on to send missionaries worldwide.

elizabeth.title: Elizabeth I Takes the Throne
elizabeth.caption: She succeeded her sister Mary I. Saying she was married to her kingdom, she never wed and led England's golden age.

voc.title: Dutch East India Company Founded
voc.caption: Called the world's first stock company, it dominated the Asian spice trade and kept a post at Dejima in Nagasaki.

jamestown.title: Jamestown Founded
jamestown.caption: England's first permanent colony in North America, also known for the story of Pocahontas.

later_jin.title: Nurhaci Founds the Later Jin
later_jin.caption: The Jurchen leader Nurhaci founded a state in Manchuria. Later renamed Qing, it came to rule China.

taj_mahal.title: Taj Mahal Begun
taj_mahal.caption: The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan began this white marble tomb for his beloved late wife.

london_fire.title: Great Fire of London
london_fire.caption: A fire from a bakery burned for four days and destroyed most of the city, which was rebuilt in brick.

seven_years.title: Seven Years' War Begins
seven_years.caption: Austria and Prussia fought over Silesia, while Britain and France fought overseas.

cook.title: Cook Reaches Eastern Australia
cook.caption: Captain Cook reached Australia's east coast and claimed it for Britain. A penal colony was later set up there.

haiti.title: Haitian Revolution Begins
haiti.caption: Enslaved Africans rose up in a French colony. Led by Toussaint Louverture, they created the first Black republic.

rosetta.title: Rosetta Stone Found
rosetta.caption: A stone found during Napoleon's Egyptian campaign. Champollion later used it to decipher hieroglyphs.

louisiana.title: Louisiana Purchase
louisiana.caption: President Jefferson bought a vast territory from Napoleon, doubling the size of the United States.

victoria.title: Queen Victoria Takes the Throne
victoria.caption: Crowned at 18, she reigned over 63 years, a symbol of the empire on which the sun never set.

gold_rush.title: California Gold Rush
gold_rush.caption: Gold was found near Sutter's Mill, and people from around the world rushed in, dreaming of riches.

crimean.title: Crimean War Begins
crimean.caption: Russia fought the Ottomans, and Britain and France joined in. It is known for Florence Nightingale's nursing.

statue_of_liberty.title: Statue of Liberty Completed
statue_of_liberty.caption: A gift from France for America's centennial, it stands at the entrance to New York Harbor.

spanish_american.title: Spanish-American War
spanish_american.caption: The US fought Spain over Cuban independence. Gaining the Philippines and more, America rose as a great power.

boxer.title: Boxer Rebellion
boxer.caption: The Boxers, vowing to support Qing and destroy foreigners, besieged the legations in Beijing. An eight-nation force including Japan crushed them.

sf_earthquake.title: San Francisco Earthquake and Fire
sf_earthquake.caption: A great quake struck early on April 18, and fires burned most of the city.

roc_founding.title: Republic of China Founded
roc_founding.caption: Sun Yat-sen became provisional president in Nanjing, creating Asia's first republic. The last Qing emperor abdicated the next month.

armistice.title: World War I Armistice
armistice.caption: At 11 a.m. on November 11, the armistice signed in a railway car in Compiegne forest took effect, ending over four years of war.

tutankhamun.title: Tomb of Tutankhamun Found
tutankhamun.caption: The Briton Howard Carter found an unlooted royal tomb in the Valley of the Kings, full of treasures like the golden mask.

normandy.title: Normandy Landings
normandy.caption: On June 6, Allied forces landed on the beaches of northern France, the largest seaborne invasion ever, hastening Germany's defeat.

india_independence.title: Indian Independence
india_independence.caption: British rule ended and Nehru became prime minister. Pakistan split off at the same time, creating vast numbers of refugees.

udhr.title: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
udhr.caption: Adopted by the UN General Assembly, it set out for the first time, in shared words for all, the rights every person is born with.

korean_war.title: Korean War Begins
korean_war.caption: North Korean troops crossed the 38th parallel into the South. The US and China joined, and the war lasted over three years.

berlin_wall_built.title: Berlin Wall Built
berlin_wall_built.caption: To stop people fleeing west, East Germany began sealing off West Berlin overnight. It became the symbol of the Cold War.

i_have_a_dream.title: "I Have a Dream" Speech
i_have_a_dream.caption: At the March on Washington, Martin Luther King Jr. spoke to some 250,000 people. The Civil Rights Act passed the next year.

oil_crisis.title: First Oil Crisis
oil_crisis.caption: Oil producers raised prices during the fourth Arab-Israeli war. In Japan, people panicked and hoarded toilet paper.

vietnam_end.title: End of the Vietnam War
vietnam_end.caption: North Vietnamese troops took Saigon, ending the war. North and South were united the next year.

chernobyl.title: Chernobyl Disaster
chernobyl.caption: Reactor 4 at a Soviet nuclear plant exploded, spreading radiation across Europe. Nearby towns are still empty.

hong_kong.title: Return of Hong Kong
hong_kong.caption: After some 150 years as a British colony, Hong Kong returned to China under "one country, two systems."

peloponnesian_end.title: End of the Peloponnesian War
peloponnesian_end.caption: Sparta forced Athens to surrender. Athens' glory was over, but Sparta's dominance did not last long either.

leuctra.title: Battle of Leuctra
leuctra.caption: Epaminondas of Thebes beat Sparta with a slanted battle line, ending Spartan supremacy.

changping.title: Battle of Changping
changping.caption: Bai Qi of Qin crushed Zhao. He is said to have buried 400,000 prisoners alive.

hannibal_alps.title: Hannibal Crosses the Alps
hannibal_alps.caption: The Carthaginian general led elephants and a great army over the Alps, outwitting Rome to enter Italy.

shihuang_death.title: Death of the First Emperor
shihuang_death.caption: The First Emperor died while touring his realm. The Terracotta Army guards his huge tomb. Qin soon fell.

triumvirate.title: First Triumvirate
triumvirate.caption: Caesar, Pompey and Crassus joined forces against the Senate in a private pact.

cleopatra.title: Death of Cleopatra
cleopatra.caption: After the defeat at Actium she took her own life, said to be by the bite of a snake, and the Ptolemaic dynasty ended.

britannia.title: Claudius Conquers Britain
britannia.caption: Emperor Claudius sent an army to Britain. Londinium, the future London, was founded.

hadrians_wall.title: Hadrian's Wall Begun
hadrians_wall.caption: A stone wall Emperor Hadrian built across northern Britain, about 118 km long, marking Rome's northern frontier.

state_religion.title: Christianity Becomes the State Religion
state_religion.caption: Emperor Theodosius made the Nicene faith the official creed of the empire, and Christianity became the state religion.

xuanzang.title: Xuanzang Returns from India
xuanzang.caption: The Tang monk Xuanzang traveled to India for Buddhist scriptures and returned to Chang'an. He inspired the monk in Journey to the West.

silla.title: Silla Unifies Korea
silla.caption: Allied with Tang, Silla defeated Baekje and Goguryeo, then drove out the Tang army and unified the peninsula.

wu_zetian.title: Wu Zetian Takes the Throne
wu_zetian.caption: The only empress regnant in Chinese history. Rising from Tang empress to ruler, she renamed the dynasty Zhou.

abbasid.title: Abbasid Caliphate Founded
abbasid.caption: Abu al-Abbas overthrew the Umayyads. Islamic culture later flowered in their capital, Baghdad.

talas.title: Battle of Talas
talas.caption: Tang and Abbasid armies clashed in Central Asia. One theory says captives carried papermaking west.

lindisfarne.title: Viking Raid on Lindisfarne
lindisfarne.caption: Vikings from the North Sea attacked a monastery in England, seen as the start of the Viking Age.

goryeo.title: Goryeo Founded
goryeo.caption: A Korean dynasty founded by Wang Geon. It reunited the peninsula, and its name is the root of the word "Korea."

manzikert.title: Battle of Manzikert
manzikert.caption: The Seljuks defeated the Byzantine army and captured its emperor, leading to the later call for the Crusades.

domesday.title: Domesday Book Compiled
domesday.caption: William I had the land and property of England surveyed and recorded in a great register.

fourth_crusade.title: Fourth Crusade Takes Constantinople
fourth_crusade.caption: Steered by Venice, the crusaders attacked the Christian Byzantine capital, looted it and set up a Latin Empire.

yamen.title: Fall of the Southern Song
yamen.caption: Yuan forces destroyed the Southern Song at Yamen. A loyal minister leapt into the sea carrying the child emperor.

wat_tyler.title: Wat Tyler's Rebellion
wat_tyler.caption: English peasants angry at a poll tax occupied London. A preacher asked who was a gentleman when Adam delved and Eve span.

joseon.title: Joseon Dynasty Founded
joseon.caption: Founded by the Goryeo general Yi Seong-gye, it lasted about 500 years with its capital at Hanseong, now Seoul.

hangul.title: Hangul Proclaimed
hangul.caption: King Sejong of Joseon proclaimed a new alphabet made for the common people. South Korea still celebrates Hangul Day.

bosworth.title: Battle of Bosworth Field
bosworth.caption: Henry Tudor defeated Richard III, ending the Wars of the Roses and beginning the Tudor dynasty.

sistine.title: Sistine Chapel Ceiling Begun
sistine.caption: Michelangelo began painting at the Pope's command. Over four years he created works like The Creation of Adam.

gregorian.title: Gregorian Calendar Adopted
gregorian.caption: Pope Gregory XIII reformed the Julian calendar. It is the calendar widely used around the world today.

don_quixote.title: Don Quixote Part One Published
don_quixote.caption: Cervantes's novel follows an old man who longs to be a knight of romance. It is called the first modern novel.

ming_fall.title: Fall of the Ming
ming_fall.caption: Li Zicheng's rebels took Beijing and the Chongzhen Emperor took his own life. Qing armies then crossed the Great Wall and ruled China.

lisbon.title: Lisbon Earthquake
lisbon.caption: On November 1 a quake, a great tsunami and fires destroyed Portugal's capital, shocking thinkers like Voltaire.

us_constitution.title: US Constitution Drafted
us_constitution.caption: Written at the convention in Philadelphia, it is one of the oldest written constitutions still in use. It set up the separation of powers.

egypt_campaign.title: Napoleon's Egyptian Campaign
egypt_campaign.caption: Napoleon tried to cut Britain's link to India. He won the Battle of the Pyramids and brought scholars along.

greek_independence.title: Greek War of Independence Begins
greek_independence.caption: Greeks rose against Ottoman rule. The poet Byron joined as a volunteer, and Greece won independence in 1829.

nanjing.title: Treaty of Nanjing
nanjing.caption: The treaty ending the Opium War. Qing gave up Hong Kong and opened five ports, its first unequal treaty.

sepoy.title: Indian Rebellion
sepoy.caption: A mutiny of the East India Company's Indian soldiers spread widely. The Mughal Empire fell the next year, and Britain began ruling India directly.

serf_emancipation.title: Emancipation of the Russian Serfs
serf_emancipation.caption: After defeat in the Crimean War, Alexander II freed the serfs, though peasants still bore heavy burdens.

emancipation.title: Emancipation Proclamation
emancipation.caption: Issued by Lincoln during the Civil War, it declared slaves in the South free and made clear what the war was for.

franco_prussian.title: Franco-Prussian War Begins
franco_prussian.caption: Bismarck's Ems telegram started the war. Napoleon III was captured, and German unification was completed.

nobel.title: First Nobel Prizes
nobel.caption: Prizes founded by the will of the inventor of dynamite. Roentgen and others were the first winners.

model_t.title: Ford Model T Goes on Sale
model_t.caption: Henry Ford's car for everyone. Assembly-line production cut its price and began the age of the automobile.

amundsen.title: Amundsen Reaches the South Pole
amundsen.caption: The Norwegian explorer beat Britain's Scott to the Pole by about a month. His plan to use dog sleds paid off.

panama.title: Panama Canal Opens
panama.caption: The US opened a canal linking the Pacific and the Atlantic, using locks to lift ships over the hills.

league.title: League of Nations Founded
league.caption: Founded at Wilson's urging, but the United States itself never joined because Congress opposed it.

yalta.title: Yalta Conference
yalta.caption: Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin met in Crimea to plan the postwar world and the Soviet entry into the war against Japan.

nato.title: NATO Founded
nato.caption: A military alliance of the US and Western Europe against the USSR. Its headquarters later moved to Brussels.

cuban_revolution.title: Cuban Revolution
cuban_revolution.caption: Castro, Guevara and others overthrew the Batista regime. Cuba later became socialist and clashed with the US.

prague_spring.title: Prague Spring
prague_spring.caption: Dubcek of Czechoslovakia pushed for freedom, but a Soviet-led invasion crushed it.

iran_revolution.title: Iranian Revolution
iran_revolution.caption: Led by Khomeini, it overthrew the Pahlavi dynasty and founded an Islamic Republic, causing the second oil crisis.

eu.title: European Union Founded
eu.caption: Born when the Maastricht Treaty took effect. The common currency, the euro, came later.

lehman.title: Lehman Shock
lehman.caption: The US investment bank Lehman Brothers collapsed, throwing world financial markets into chaos.

assyria_fall.title: Fall of Nineveh
assyria_fall.caption: Babylonian and Median armies took the Assyrian capital, and the empire that had united the Near East collapsed.

delian_league.title: Delian League Formed
delian_league.caption: Formed under Athens to guard against Persia's return. It later became a tool of Athenian rule.

pericles_death.title: Death of Pericles
pericles_death.caption: The leader of Athens at its height died in a plague during the Peloponnesian War.

philip2_death.title: Assassination of Philip II
philip2_death.caption: The Macedonian king was killed at his daughter's wedding. His son Alexander became king at 20.

issus.title: Battle of Issus
issus.caption: Alexander the Great defeated Darius III, a battle shown in a famous mosaic from Pompeii.

ipsus.title: Battle of Ipsus
ipsus.caption: In the wars among Alexander's successors, Antigonus was killed. The breakup of the empire became final.

punic2.title: Second Punic War Begins
punic2.caption: Hannibal invaded Italy. Rome suffered, but won in the end and became the great power of the Mediterranean.

pydna.title: Battle of Pydna
pydna.caption: The Roman army crushed the Macedonians, showing the legion's strength over the phalanx.

corinth_destruction.title: Destruction of Corinth
corinth_destruction.caption: Rome defeated the Achaean League and razed the Greek city, in the same year Carthage fell.

sulla_dictator.title: Sulla Becomes Dictator
sulla_dictator.caption: Victorious in civil war, Sulla became dictator with no time limit. He purged his enemies and tried to restore the Senate's power.

alesia.title: Battle of Alesia
alesia.caption: Caesar besieged and forced the surrender of the Gallic leader Vercingetorix, sealing the conquest of Gaul.

pharsalus.title: Battle of Pharsalus
pharsalus.caption: Caesar defeated Pompey, who fled to Egypt and was killed there.

julian_calendar.title: Julian Calendar
julian_calendar.caption: Caesar adopted the Egyptian solar calendar, adding a leap year every four years.

philippi.title: Battle of Philippi
philippi.caption: Antony and Octavian defeated Brutus and the other assassins of Caesar.

wang_mang.title: Wang Mang Founds Xin
wang_mang.caption: Wang Mang, a relative of the Han empresses, seized the throne. He idealized the Zhou system, but fell to the Red Eyebrows revolt.

augustus_death.title: Death of Augustus
augustus_death.caption: The first Roman emperor died, said to have boasted that he found Rome brick and left it marble. August is named after him.

jerusalem_70.title: Romans Destroy Jerusalem
jerusalem_70.caption: In the Jewish War, Titus destroyed the city and its Temple. The Western Wall is a remnant of that Temple.

kan_ei.title: Gan Ying Sent Toward Rome
kan_ei.caption: The general Ban Chao sent Gan Ying west toward Rome. He reached near the Persian Gulf but turned back without crossing the sea.

trajan_max.title: Trajan Conquers Dacia
trajan_max.caption: Emperor Trajan conquered what is now Romania, bringing the Roman Empire close to its greatest size.

marcus_aurelius.title: Marcus Aurelius Becomes Emperor
marcus_aurelius.caption: The last of the Five Good Emperors, known as the philosopher emperor who wrote his Meditations on campaign.

antonine_edict.title: Edict of Caracalla
antonine_edict.caption: Emperor Caracalla granted Roman citizenship to all free people of the empire, perhaps to raise more taxes.

diocletian.title: Diocletian Becomes Emperor
diocletian.caption: He ended the age of soldier emperors and set up rule by four emperors. He also led a great persecution of Christians.

milvian_bridge.title: Battle of the Milvian Bridge
milvian_bridge.caption: Constantine defeated Maxentius. Before the battle he is said to have seen a vision of the cross.

adrianople.title: Battle of Adrianople
adrianople.caption: The Visigoths routed a Roman army, and Emperor Valens was killed. Germanic power began to shake the empire.

hun_attila.title: Death of Attila
hun_attila.caption: The Hun king, feared as the "Scourge of God," died suddenly on his wedding night. His empire quickly fell apart.

benedict.title: Monte Cassino Founded
benedict.caption: St. Benedict's monastery in Italy. His rule, "pray and work," became the model for Western monasteries.

gregory_great.title: Gregory the Great Becomes Pope
gregory_great.caption: He laid the base of medieval papal power and sent missionaries to England. Gregorian chant bears his name.

grand_canal.title: Grand Canal Opens
grand_canal.caption: Emperor Yang of Sui built a canal linking north China and the Yangtze. Its harsh labor hastened Sui's fall, but it became a vital trade route.

tang_taizong.title: Emperor Taizong of Tang Takes the Throne
tang_taizong.caption: Li Shimin seized power by killing his brother at the Xuanwu Gate. His reign is remembered as an ideal of good government.

mecca_conquest.title: Muhammad Takes Mecca
mecca_conquest.caption: Muhammad entered Mecca with 10,000 men without a fight. The idols of the Kaaba were destroyed.

muhammad_death.title: Death of Muhammad
muhammad_death.caption: The Prophet of Islam died in Medina. Abu Bakr became the first caliph, and the great Arab conquests began.

nahavand.title: Battle of Nahavand
nahavand.caption: Arab Muslim forces defeated the Sasanian Persian army, and the Sasanian Empire effectively fell.

tibet_wencheng.title: Princess Wencheng Goes to Tibet
tibet_wencheng.caption: A Tang princess married the Tibetan king Songtsen Gampo. She is said to have brought Buddhism and Tang culture to Tibet.

karbala.title: Battle of Karbala
karbala.caption: Husayn, grandson of Muhammad, was killed by an Umayyad army. Shia Muslims still mourn this day.

islam_spain.title: Muslims Land in Iberia
islam_spain.caption: A Muslim army under Tariq crossed the strait and destroyed the Visigothic kingdom. Gibraltar is named after him.

pepin_king.title: Pepin Crowned King
pepin_king.caption: Pepin, son of Charles Martel, became king with the Pope's support and founded the Carolingian dynasty.

pepin_donation.title: Donation of Pepin
pepin_donation.caption: Pepin gave the Pope lands taken from the Lombards, the start of the Papal States.

cordoba_mosque.title: Great Mosque of Cordoba Begun
cordoba_mosque.caption: Begun in Cordoba, capital of the Umayyads of Spain. It is famous for its forest of red and white horseshoe arches.

alfred_great.title: Alfred the Great Becomes King
alfred_great.caption: The king of Wessex held back the Danish invaders. He is the only English king called "the Great."

tang_fall.title: Fall of the Tang
tang_fall.caption: The general Zhu Quanzhong took the throne and founded the Later Liang. The 300-year Tang ended, and an age of division began.

cluny.title: Cluny Abbey Founded
cluny.caption: A monastery founded in Burgundy, France. It became the center of a movement to reform the Church.

lechfeld.title: Battle of Lechfeld
lechfeld.caption: King Otto I of Germany defeated the Magyars, ending their raids into Western Europe.

hugh_capet.title: Capetian Dynasty Begins
hugh_capet.caption: Hugh Capet was elected king of France. The direct Capetian line lasted until the 14th century.

seljuk_baghdad.title: Seljuks Enter Baghdad
seljuk_baghdad.caption: Tughril Beg entered Baghdad and received the title of sultan from the Abbasid caliph.

wang_anshi.title: Wang Anshi's New Policies
wang_anshi.caption: Under Emperor Shenzong of Northern Song, Wang Anshi tried to fix finances and the army. Conservatives like Sima Guang opposed him.

jerusalem_1099.title: Crusaders Take Jerusalem
jerusalem_1099.caption: The First Crusade captured Jerusalem and massacred many of its people. The Kingdom of Jerusalem was founded.

worms_concordat.title: Concordat of Worms
worms_concordat.caption: It settled the fight between emperor and pope over appointing bishops, and helped German princes grow stronger.

second_crusade.title: Second Crusade
second_crusade.caption: Led by Louis VII of France and Conrad III of Germany, it ended with a failed siege of Damascus.

hattin.title: Battle of Hattin
hattin.caption: Saladin crushed the main crusader army, opening the way to retake Jerusalem.

third_crusade.title: Third Crusade
third_crusade.caption: Richard the Lionheart and others fought Saladin. They could not retake the Holy City, and a truce was made.

delhi_sultanate.title: Delhi Sultanate Founded
delhi_sultanate.caption: Aibak, a general who had been a slave, founded a dynasty in Delhi, the first Islamic dynasty of India.

albigensian.title: Albigensian Crusade
albigensian.caption: The Pope called for a crusade against the Cathar heretics of southern France. In the end, royal power spread south.

bouvines.title: Battle of Bouvines
bouvines.caption: Philip II of France beat Emperor Otto IV and his English allies. King John, who lost his lands in France, grew weaker.

khwarazm.title: Mongol Invasion of Khwarazm
khwarazm.caption: After a caravan was massacred, Genghis Khan invaded Central Asia. Its cities were utterly destroyed.

jin_fall.title: Fall of the Jin
jin_fall.caption: The Jurchen Jin dynasty fell to the Mongols and the Southern Song, in the reign of Ogedei Khan.

batu_kiev.title: Mongols Take Kiev
batu_kiev.caption: Batu's army stormed Kiev. The Russian principalities came under the rule of the Golden Horde.

ain_jalut.title: Battle of Ain Jalut
ain_jalut.caption: The Mamluk army of Egypt defeated the Mongols, halting their westward advance.

yuan_name.title: Yuan Dynasty Named
yuan_name.caption: Kublai Khan gave his state the Chinese name "Great Yuan." His capital, Dadu, grew into modern Beijing.

model_parliament.title: Model Parliament
model_parliament.caption: Edward I of England summoned clergy, nobles and town representatives. It became the model for later parliaments.

estates_general.title: First Estates-General
estates_general.caption: Philip IV of France, at odds with the Pope, gathered clergy, nobles and commoners, the start of France's assembly of estates.

avignon.title: Papacy Moves to Avignon
avignon.caption: Under French influence, the papal court moved to Avignon. It stayed about 70 years, and papal authority weakened.

bannockburn.title: Battle of Bannockburn
bannockburn.caption: King Robert the Bruce of Scotland defeated the English, securing Scotland's independence.

crecy.title: Battle of Crecy
crecy.caption: In the Hundred Years' War, English longbowmen shattered the French knights, signaling the end of the age of knights.

black_death.title: Black Death Reaches Europe
black_death.caption: It came to Italy on ships from the Black Sea and killed about a third of Europe's people, transforming society.

jacquerie.title: Jacquerie
jacquerie.caption: Peasants in northern France, suffering from the Hundred Years' War, rose in revolt. "Jacques" was a scornful name for peasants.

golden_bull.title: Golden Bull
golden_bull.caption: Emperor Charles IV's law for electing the Holy Roman Emperor, confirming the rights of seven electors.

schism_1378.title: Western Schism Begins
schism_1378.caption: Rival popes reigned in Rome and Avignon. The split was healed later by the Council of Constance.

kalmar_union.title: Kalmar Union
kalmar_union.caption: Under Margaret I of Denmark, the three Nordic kingdoms were joined under one crown.

yongle_beijing.title: Ming Capital Moved to Beijing
yongle_beijing.caption: The Yongle Emperor moved the capital from Nanjing to Beijing. The Forbidden City he completed still stands.

constance.title: Council of Constance Opens
constance.caption: The council ended the Western Schism. It condemned Jan Hus as a heretic and had him burned.

hus_death.title: Jan Hus Burned at the Stake
hus_death.caption: The Bohemian reformer was condemned as a heretic by the council and burned, setting off the Hussite Wars.

joan_death.title: Joan of Arc Burned at the Stake
joan_death.caption: Captured by the English, Joan was burned as a heretic in Rouen at 19. She was later made a saint.

tumu.title: Tumu Crisis
tumu.caption: The Ming Zhengtong Emperor was captured by Esen of the Oirats, and Ming power declined.

hundred_end.title: End of the Hundred Years' War
hundred_end.caption: With the fall of Bordeaux, England lost almost all its lands in France, and the long war ended.

roses.title: Wars of the Roses Begin
roses.caption: The houses of Lancaster and York fought for the throne for 30 years, ending with the Tudor dynasty.

ivan3.title: Ivan III Ends Mongol Rule
ivan3.caption: In a standoff on the Ugra River, the Grand Prince of Moscow made the Mongol army withdraw, ending the "Tatar yoke."

cabot.title: Cabot Reaches North America
cabot.caption: Sent by the English king, he reached the east coast of North America, said to be the first European there since the Vikings.

cabral.title: Cabral Reaches Brazil
cabral.caption: A Portuguese fleet bound for India was carried west and reached Brazil, which was claimed for Portugal.

safavid.title: Safavid Dynasty Founded
safavid.caption: Ismail I founded a dynasty in Iran. Making Shia Islam the state religion, it laid the foundation of modern Iran.

david_statue.title: Michelangelo's David Completed
david_statue.caption: Michelangelo carved it from a huge block of marble. It was placed as a symbol of the Florentine Republic.

st_peters.title: Rebuilding of St. Peter's Begun
st_peters.caption: Pope Julius II began rebuilding the basilica. Indulgences sold to pay for it drew Luther's attack.

utopia.title: Thomas More's Utopia
utopia.caption: The English thinker described the society of an imaginary island. Its title still means an ideal place.

charles5.title: Charles V Elected Emperor
charles5.caption: King Charles I of Spain was elected Holy Roman Emperor. Habsburg lands now spread across the globe.

worms_diet.title: Diet of Worms
worms_diet.caption: Before Charles V, Luther refused to take back his views and was outlawed. The Elector of Saxony hid him.

magellan_return.title: Magellan's Fleet Returns
magellan_return.caption: Elcano led the 18 survivors back to Spain, completing the first voyage around the world.

panipat1.title: First Battle of Panipat
panipat1.caption: Babur used firearms to beat the large Lodi army, laying the foundation of the Mughal Empire.

mohacs.title: Battle of Mohacs
mohacs.caption: Suleiman I of the Ottomans crushed the Hungarian army, and the king was killed. Most of Hungary fell to the empire.

sack_rome.title: Sack of Rome
sack_rome.caption: Mercenaries of Charles V looted Rome. The city, heart of the Renaissance, was ruined, and its high period ended.

supremacy.title: Church of England Founded
supremacy.caption: Clashing with the Pope over his divorce, Henry VIII made himself head of the English Church.

calvin.title: Calvin's Institutes
calvin.caption: The French reformer's main work, setting out predestination. He later led reform in Geneva.

akbar.title: Akbar Takes the Throne
akbar.caption: The third Mughal emperor came to the throne at 13. He ended the tax on Hindus and opened the empire's golden age.

st_bartholomew.title: St. Bartholomew's Day Massacre
st_bartholomew.caption: Catholics in Paris massacred Huguenots, intensifying the French Wars of Religion.

utrecht_union.title: Union of Utrecht
utrecht_union.caption: Seven northern provinces of the Netherlands allied against Spain, the base of Dutch independence.

dutch_independence.title: Dutch Declaration of Independence
dutch_independence.caption: The northern Netherlands rejected the rule of Philip II of Spain. Independence was recognized in 1648.

hamlet_globe.title: Globe Theatre Opens
hamlet_globe.caption: A theater on the south bank of the Thames in London, where many of Shakespeare's plays were performed.

qing_name.title: Qing Dynasty Named
qing_name.caption: Hong Taiji renamed the Later Jin as Qing and became emperor, ruler of Manchus, Mongols and Han.

english_civil.title: English Civil War Begins
english_civil.caption: War broke out between King Charles I and Parliament. Cromwell's Ironsides made their name.

tasman.title: Tasman Reaches New Zealand
tasman.caption: The Dutch navigator reached New Zealand, named after the Dutch province of Zeeland.

navigation_act.title: Navigation Act
navigation_act.caption: A law of Cromwell's England aimed at Dutch carrying trade. It led to the Anglo-Dutch Wars.

cape_colony.title: Cape Colony Founded
cape_colony.caption: Van Riebeeck of the Dutch East India Company set up a supply station at Africa's southern tip. It later became British.

restoration.title: English Restoration
restoration.caption: After Cromwell's death, Charles II became king and the monarchy was restored.

new_amsterdam.title: New Amsterdam Becomes English
new_amsterdam.caption: England seized the Dutch colony and renamed it New York after the Duke of York.

kangxi_sanfan.title: Revolt of the Three Feudatories
kangxi_sanfan.caption: Han Chinese princes such as Wu Sangui rebelled against Qing. The Kangxi Emperor crushed them and secured Qing rule.

taiwan_qing.title: Qing Takes Taiwan
taiwan_qing.caption: The Zheng regime surrendered, and Taiwan became Qing territory under Fujian province.

nantes_revocation.title: Revocation of the Edict of Nantes
nantes_revocation.caption: Louis XIV revoked the Edict, and many Huguenots fled abroad, a blow to French industry.

bill_of_rights.title: English Bill of Rights
bill_of_rights.caption: Passed in the Glorious Revolution, it banned taxes without Parliament's consent, the basis of Britain's constitutional monarchy.

bank_england.title: Bank of England Founded
bank_england.caption: Created to fund the war with France, it later became the model for central banks worldwide.

prussia_kingdom.title: Kingdom of Prussia Founded
prussia_kingdom.caption: The Elector of Brandenburg won the title of king for backing the emperor. Prussia later led German unification.

spanish_succession.title: War of the Spanish Succession
spanish_succession.caption: Austria, Britain and others opposed Louis XIV's grandson inheriting the Spanish throne.

great_britain.title: Kingdom of Great Britain Formed
great_britain.caption: The parliaments of England and Scotland were joined, creating the Kingdom of Great Britain.

poltava.title: Battle of Poltava
poltava.caption: Peter the Great of Russia defeated Charles XII of Sweden, and Russia became the great power of the Baltic.

utrecht_treaty.title: Treaty of Utrecht
utrecht_treaty.caption: The peace ending the War of the Spanish Succession. Britain gained Gibraltar and moved closer to ruling the seas.

south_sea.title: South Sea Bubble
south_sea.caption: Shares of Britain's South Sea Company soared, then crashed, one origin of the word "bubble." Even Newton lost heavily.

kyakhta.title: Treaty of Kyakhta
kyakhta.caption: Qing and Russia fixed the Mongolian border and agreed to trade at Kyakhta.

austrian_succession.title: War of the Austrian Succession
austrian_succession.caption: Many states challenged Maria Theresa's inheritance, and Prussia seized Silesia.

encyclopedie.title: The Encyclopedie Begins
encyclopedie.caption: An encyclopedia edited by Diderot and d'Alembert. Gathering the knowledge of its time, it spread Enlightenment ideas.

diplomatic_revolution.title: Diplomatic Revolution
diplomatic_revolution.caption: Old enemies Austria and France became allies, which also led to Marie Antoinette's marriage.

canton_system.title: Qing Limits Trade to Canton
canton_system.caption: The Qianlong Emperor restricted Western trade to Canton. Frustration over trade helped lead to the Opium War.

quebec.title: Battle of the Plains of Abraham
quebec.caption: British troops beat the French outside Quebec, and both generals were killed. Canada became British.

paris_1763.title: Treaty of Paris (1763)
paris_1763.caption: The peace ending the Seven Years' War. France lost most of North America, and Britain's overseas dominance was sealed.

social_contract.title: Rousseau's The Social Contract
social_contract.caption: Rousseau's book on popular sovereignty became an intellectual pillar of the French Revolution.

catherine2.title: Catherine the Great Takes the Throne
catherine2.caption: A German-born empress pushed aside her husband Peter III to rule. As an enlightened despot she expanded Russia.

stamp_act.title: Stamp Act
stamp_act.caption: Britain taxed documents in the colonies. Protests of "no taxation without representation" got it repealed the next year.

poland_partition1.title: First Partition of Poland
poland_partition1.caption: Russia, Prussia and Austria seized Polish lands. After three partitions, Poland vanished.

pugachev.title: Pugachev's Rebellion
pugachev.caption: The Cossack Pugachev, claiming to be Peter III, rose up with peasants. Catherine the Great crushed the revolt.

lexington.title: Battles of Lexington and Concord
lexington.caption: British troops clashed with colonial militia, the first battles of the American Revolution.

wealth_nations.title: Adam Smith's The Wealth of Nations
wealth_nations.caption: Smith's book explained the division of labor and the "invisible hand," founding modern economics.

yorktown.title: Battle of Yorktown
yorktown.caption: Washington and French allies forced the British to surrender, effectively winning American independence.

paris_1783.title: Treaty of Paris (1783)
paris_1783.caption: Britain recognized American independence. The lands east of the Mississippi became US territory.

washington_president.title: Washington Becomes President
washington_president.caption: The commander of the Revolution became the first president. He stepped down after two terms, setting a lasting example.

rights_of_man.title: Declaration of the Rights of Man
rights_of_man.caption: Adopted by the National Assembly during the French Revolution, it proclaimed liberty, equality and popular sovereignty.

varennes.title: Flight to Varennes
varennes.caption: The royal family tried to flee Paris and was caught. Trust in the king collapsed, and calls for a republic grew.

first_republic.title: French First Republic Proclaimed
first_republic.caption: The National Convention abolished the monarchy, the day after the victory at Valmy.

thermidor.title: Thermidorian Reaction
thermidor.caption: Robespierre, leader of the Terror, was overthrown and executed. The Revolution's radical turn came to a halt.

brumaire.title: Coup of 18 Brumaire
brumaire.caption: Back from Egypt, Napoleon overthrew the Directory and set up the Consulate, seen as the end of the French Revolution.

napoleonic_code.title: Napoleonic Code
napoleonic_code.caption: France's civil code, setting equality before the law and the protection of property. Many nations copied it.

haiti_independence.title: Haitian Independence
haiti_independence.caption: Dessalines declared independence, making Haiti the first free nation in Latin America and the first Black republic.

austerlitz.title: Battle of Austerlitz
austerlitz.caption: Napoleon defeated the Austrians and Russians, a clash also called the Battle of the Three Emperors.

rhine_confederation.title: Confederation of the Rhine
rhine_confederation.caption: Southwestern German states united under Napoleon's protection, and the Holy Roman Empire came to an end.

continental_blockade.title: Continental System
continental_blockade.caption: Napoleon's Berlin Decree banned European trade with Britain, but Russia refused to go along.

slave_trade_abolition.title: Britain Abolishes the Slave Trade
slave_trade_abolition.caption: After a campaign led by Wilberforce and others, Parliament voted to ban the slave trade.

fulton.title: Fulton's Steamboat
fulton.caption: An American engineer ran the steamboat Clermont on the Hudson River, the first commercial success with steam.

leipzig.title: Battle of Leipzig
leipzig.caption: An allied coalition defeated Napoleon in the "Battle of the Nations." He gave up his throne the next year.

monroe.title: Monroe Doctrine
monroe.caption: President Monroe declared that Europe and the Americas should stay out of each other's affairs, long a basis of US policy.

decembrist.title: Decembrist Revolt
decembrist.caption: Liberal officers rose up when Nicholas I took the throne and were crushed, forerunners of Russia's revolutionaries.

belgium.title: Belgian Independence
belgium.caption: Inspired by the July Revolution in France, Belgium broke away from the Netherlands and later became permanently neutral.

reform_act.title: Great Reform Act
